detail.abstract: The significant increases in the worldwide volumes and complexity of online advertisements have highlighted difficulties in pricing and scheduling such adverts. The autonomy of these Online Advertising Networks (OANs) and the increasing volumes of both legal and illegal online filesharing further complicates matters and can increase Traffic-delays and Network-Instability. This article: i) introduces new online advertising models (that can be coded as Algorithms) that solve problems inherent in existing advertising models (eg. Auctions, price-discovery, scheduling, HCI-problems, UI/UX, energy-efficiency, Uncertainty, reduced sustainability; etc.); ii) explains why current internet ads cannot be accurately valued using any known methods; iii) explains why auctions of online advertising are inefficient, inaccurate and can result in Herd Mentality which is detrimental to many companies.

title: Quantifying Product/Service Value: A Framework for Modeling Perceived Value to Pricing

detail.title: Quantifying Product/Service Value: A Framework for Modeling Perceived Value to Pricing
detail.abstract: Value has long been recognized as a central yet elusive construct in marketing and strategy. While prior research has conceptualized value as a trade-off between quality and sacrifice (Zeithaml, 1988), an experiential phenomenon (Holbrook, 1999), or as co-created in use (Vargo & Lusch, 2004), existing approaches remain fragmented and often lack operational precision. This paper introduces a layered framework designed to quantify product and service value in a structured, multi-dimensional manner. The proposed framework integrates three layers of analysis. The first layer captures intrinsic value, derived from frequency of need, intensity of need, and strategic exclusivity. The second layer accounts for perceived value adjustments, incorporating differentiation effects and positioning along the necessity-indulgence-luxury continuum. The third layer assesses affordability and pricing, translating potential value into realized adoption by adjusting for income distribution, socioeconomic reach, and benchmark price indices. Together, these layers generate a universal scoring system (1-1000), enabling comparisons across industries, markets, and cultural contexts. The paper situates this framework within established literature on consumer value, pricing, and socioeconomic segmentation while advancing theoretical integration. It develops a series of conceptual propositions regarding the relationships between intrinsic drivers, perception-based adjustments, and affordability filters. Practical implications are outlined for managers seeking to optimize pricing, positioning, and resource allocation, while policy implications highlight the role of affordability in ensuring access to essential goods and services. By providing both a theoretical synthesis and a practical tool, the framework addresses a long-standing gap between abstract conceptualizations of value and actionable measurement. It offers pathways for future empirical validation, cross-cultural research, and integration into marketing education. Ultimately, this contribution underscores that value is not fixed but dynamically shaped by context, perception, and affordability.

title: International Peers in Higher Education and Domestic Students' Outcomes

detail.title: International Peers in Higher Education and Domestic Students' Outcomes
detail.abstract: Recent decades witnessed a rapid increase in foreign post-secondary student enrollment in the US, substantially altering the college landscape. While evidence suggests that foreign students contribute significantly to university revenues and the host economy, there remains much debate around their impact on domestic students' outcomes. Using rich administrative and survey data from a large US public university, this paper explores the effects of exposure to foreign peers in college courses on domestic students' academic outcomes. I focus on first-term introductory math courses and leverage plausibly exogenous variation in the share of foreign peers across terms but within a course-instructor pair. I find that exposure to foreign peers in lower-ability (non-calculus) courses has a sizable negative effect on the graduation rate of domestic students; students in higher-ability (calculus-based) courses are unaffected by their foreign peers. The decline in graduation comes through a drop in students graduating with non-STEM degrees, with no effect on the number of STEM graduates. Further, the negative effects are incurred by domestic students of all races except Asians; domestic Asian students incur positive effects. Exploring potential mechanisms, I find suggestive evidence of limited interaction, lack of shared interests or culture, and language barriers between domestic and foreign students. Additionally, evidence points to the potential role of domestic students' lower academic rank in their peer group. At the same time, I do not find evidence of negative social preferences associated with races or immigrants among domestic students, nor do I find evidence linking the effect to differences in abilities between domestic and foreign students.

detail.abstract: This assessment utilizes a new research method. The author, Eric Coyle, has professional experience with social listening for market research in addition to some academic knowledge building SEMs. The author seeks to combine their “real-world” knowledge of social media in combination with academic prowess using SEMs to further social listening capabilities for the greater good. The purpose of this study is to show how to potentially perform SEM (Structural Equation Modeling) using [sample] social listening data on the social media platform X, formerly known as Twitter. This study uses a methodology previously proposed; however, not necessarily tested for functionality to look at causal relationships using social media analysis. Examining causal relationships through SEM can catapult social listening analysis into an echelon of greater functionality in the age of AI (Artificial Intelligence), machine learning and natural language processing. Historically, social media data has been aggregated for review as a leading indicator and to construct simple averages and regression albeit from specific venues (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, blogs, etc…). Social media data can be collected but lacks causality analysis capability that other market research methods (e.g. survey analysis) offer, specifically through SEM. SEMs are typically built out using survey data. This assessment suggests streamlining social listening text-based data processes (and other similar input like voice transcripts converted into text) for eventual adaptation through SEM. This overture is original by way of being the first known scheme a) actually collecting, aggregating and analyzing social listening data, albeit with an AI generated data set based on messages about the brand Disney potentially found on the social media X, to build a test causal model converting social media data for use to build an actual SEM through b) illustrating a way to expand social listening beyond solely text-based analysis or venue-specific constraints while c) exhibiting how to build a SEM using social listening data within the business and marketing realm. The knowledge gap fulfilled advocates using SEM techniques in a way to expand future real-world social media research prospects. Furthermore, this analysis builds upon existing literature around challenges building SEMs with data sets with high percentages of missing high percentages of values while assessing data imputation methods to address missing values for SEM for future study. Past similar research does not provide adequate ways to replicate studies. As a result, a video series detailing methodology is available for public view on YouTube. Both a QR code and link to the video series are featured in Appendix I. This study shows that it is feasible to build a SEM using social listening data. Better indicator assessment, enhanced data imputation methods and improved data collection practices will continue to lend toward more desirable results.

detail.abstract: This article examines the role of the private sector in addressing the STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) focused green skills gap, one of the most systemic obstacles to achieving global net-zero targets. To this end, the online presence and skill development strategies of key actors (RWE and DRAX) in the UK's green energy sector are thematically and comparatively analyzed. It is determined that RWE has adopted a structured and programmatic "strategic talent pipeline" model, directly aligned with its future technology portfolio (offshore wind, hydrogen, Carbon Capture and Storage-CCS). In contrast, DRAX implements a broader, community-focused, and philanthropic "ecosystem development" model through the DRAX Foundation in its operational regions. The thematic analysis reveals convergences and divergences between these two corporate strategies across themes of vision and leadership, corporate structure and financial management, inspiration and inclusion, educational investments and their impact on the future workforce, and stakeholder engagement and collaboration. The article concludes by discussing the role and limitations of these corporate interventions in closing the national skills gap and emphasizing the necessity of a more integrated policy framework among government, industry, and educational institutions.

detail.abstract: In today's competitive global marketplace, businesses of all sizes need to improve their operational and marketing performance to survive and thrive. This study aims to explore the predictive relationship between operational costs, promotional costs, and sales volume. The secondary data analyzed were obtained from the financial statements of four SMEs in the Indonesian context. The regression model used was panel data estimated using Eviews v.12. The panel data regression model analysis, with the REM approach as the selected model, was conducted through a series of tests, namely the Chow test, the Hausman test, and the LM test. The study findings indicate that operational costs have a significant positive effect on sales volume. Promotion costs also have a significant positive effect on sales volume. Variations in the relationship between operational costs and promotional costs have a joint influence that can explain variance of sales volume, with strong predictive power. The findings of this study can fill an existing gap, relevant panel data regression models are applied to quantitative data for sales forecasting to reveal evidence that operational costs and promotional costs are important predictors of sales volume among SMEs.

detail.abstract:
The Planificador de Éxito by InspirArte introduces a practical and visually inspiring method designed to help individuals transform ideas into tangible achievements. Structured around a twelve-task methodology, the planner guides users through the processes of goal-setting, prioritization, organization, and progress tracking. Beyond time management, it emphasizes clarity of purpose, efficient resource allocation, and adaptability to changing circumstances.

Enriched with photographs of Parque La Llovizna in Ciudad Guayana, Venezuela, the planner integrates visual inspiration with strategic planning, fostering both motivation and discipline. By combining structured techniques with cultural and aesthetic elements, the Planificador de Éxito provides a holistic tool for enhancing productivity, meeting deadlines, and achieving personal and professional objectives.

detail.abstract: This project introduces Card Generator, a tool built for real-world use that automatically creates logos and cards. The system uses a React (Vite) website, a Node.js service that works with Gemini to improve prompts, and a Python FastAPI service that sends image requests to various AI backends like Hugging Face, Stability.ai, or a local diffusion setup. Beyond just creating images, the platform focuses on reliability and smooth operation. It includes features like handling jobs in the background, showing previews before applying changes, retrying failed requests with smart delays, switching to alternative providers if one fails, and tracking performance. In tests, Card Generator performs better than systems that rely on a single provider, reducing errors and response times while keeping the user experience smooth.

detail.abstract: The State of SupTech Report 2024 is the global benchmark for understanding how financial authorities adopt and scale supervisory technology. This third edition draws on data from 136 financial authorities, 23 suptech solution providers, and a longitudinal sample of 221 agencies across 144 jurisdictions. detail.title: Liquid Equity Rewards
detail.abstract:
This article develops and evaluates Liquid Equity Rewards (LER), a mechanism that links capital formation and loyalty by issuing time-weighted, utility-only rewards to verified holders of equities or cryptoassets. Drawing on the evolution of stablecoins, DeFi "liquid staking," and the post-metaverse pivot toward tokenized rewards, the paper proposes a bifurcated LER architecture: (i) voucher-based rewards for brokerage-held equities and (ii) programmable, on-chain reward units for tokenized equities. Methodologically, the analysis synthesizes market evidence on stablecoin adoption, compares LER to incumbent loyalty and yield models, and assesses regulatory fit under emerging U.S. stablecoin rules and the EU's MiCA framework.

The paper advances four contributions. First, it specifies a smart-contract design for time-weighted accrual without lockups, minimizing speculative features while preserving liquidity. Second, it articulates issuer incentives and accounting treatment that fund rewards from marketing budgets rather than creating deferred-revenue liabilities typical of points programs. Third, it outlines verification pipelines for both off-chain equities and on-chain tokenized assets, enabling compliance-aligned attribution with minimal data exposure. Fourth, it sizes the market opportunity in the context of the global rotation from fixed income to risk assets and the convergence of payments and loyalty infrastructure.

Findings indicate that LER can reduce holder churn, increase merchant throughput, and improve issuer capital efficiency while maintaining a “risk-lite” profile relative to yield-bearing crypto instruments. Policy and implementation risks persist (e.g., evolving securities and stablecoin standards), but the framework demonstrates a practical path to democratized, programmable “dividend-like” utilities across commerce and capital markets.

detail.title: Creative Currency Octaves and Public Trust Foundations: An Integrated Framework for Poverty Elimination and Economic Stabilization
detail.abstract: Creative Currency Octaves (CCO) represents an innovative economic framework that combines mathematically progressive benefit structures with Public Trust Foundations (PTF) to achieve comprehensive poverty elimination and economic stabilization. This paper presents a complete theoretical model integrating three mathematical progressions: octave doubling (2^n), conversion multipliers (1-9x), and phi rate enhancement (1.618x), alongside community wealth-building institutions. Through Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000+ iterations and comparative policy analysis, we demonstrate that while CCO alone achieves 85% poverty reduction with median wealth improvements to $37,000, the integrated CCO-PTF system achieves 98% poverty reduction with median wealth of $82,000. The framework includes deflation-inducing merchant incentives, selective participation protocols that function alongside traditional markets, and cyber-resilience mechanisms supporting 2-3 days personal reserves and 2-3 weeks household reserves. Stress testing across recession, inflation, unemployment, and climate crisis scenarios validates system stability under various participation rates. This research contributes to alternative currency literature by demonstrating how mathematical progression-based benefits can be integrated with community wealth-building institutions to create scalable poverty elimination mechanisms while maintaining economic stability and resilience.

detail.abstract: This study analyzes a modified dictatorship game in which, before splitting a fixed endowment, dictators are informed about the amount their recipients would have kept for themselves had they been assigned the role of allocators. We posit that dictators will selectively use the additional information and exploit a moral wiggle room-they will keep a larger amount when they face recipients who would have behaved more selfishly than themselves and ignore the knowledge in case of more benevolent recipients. We ran an experiment with treatment and control sessions, giving dictators information regarding potential recipients only in the former. Our experimental findings support our hypotheses, which suggest that dictators' decisions are driven not just by their idiosyncratic preferences for fairness but also by those of others. Our paper contributes to the literature on subtle contextual cues that adversely affect the prosocial behavior of dictators.

detail.title: Draft Preprint: No10 Theory
detail.abstract: This paper introduces No10 Theory, a novel framework to understand systemic collapse under conditions of extreme simultaneity. While the concept of polycrisis (Tooze, 2022) highlights overlapping and interacting crises, and black swan theory (Taleb, 2007) emphasizes rare highimpact events, both fail to capture a more radical state: the absolute concurrence of ten systemic crises across economic, social, political, and technological domains. We define No10 as a reverse Big Bang of global ordera condition where financial collapse, geopolitical conflict, pandemics, climate shocks, technological disruption, and institutional failure converge simultaneously. The theory is structured around the three-phase dynamic Shock-Erosion-Rewrite, describing how systems collapse under concurrent shocks, erode over 3-10 years, and are eventually rewritten by survivors. By analyzing historical fragments of crisis (1929 Depression, 1973 Oil Shock, 2008 Financial Crisis, 2020 Pandemic, etc.), we argue that each represents only a partial dimension of No10. Probability modeling suggests a non-negligible 1-5% chance of No10 within the next 30 years. The framework offers implications for individuals, firms, and nations in building cognitive and institutional immune systems against extreme simultaneity.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了No10理论，这是一个理解极端同时性条件下系统性崩溃的新框架。该理论描述了金融崩溃、地缘政治冲突、疫情、气候冲击、技术颠覆和制度失败同时发生的状态，并提出了Shock-Erosion-Rewrite三阶段动态模型。

AI.theoretical_framework: No10理论框架，基于Shock-Erosion-Rewrite三阶段动态模型：冲击-侵蚀-重写。该框架整合了多重危机理论（Tooze, 2022）和黑天鹅理论（Taleb, 2007）的见解，但超越了它们的局限性。
AI.method: 通过分析历史危机片段（1929年大萧条、1973年石油危机、2008年金融危机、2020年疫情等）进行理论构建，并使用概率建模来评估No10在未来30年内发生的可能性。

AI.theory_contributions: 提出了一个理解极端同时性条件下系统性崩溃的新理论框架No10，超越了现有理论的局限性，提供了更全面的分析工具。
AI.practical_contributions: 为个人、企业和国家提供了构建认知和制度免疫系统的指导，以应对极端同时性条件，增强系统韧性。

detail.title: Do Firms Voluntarily Respond to Local Social Issues? Evidence from Shocks to the Female Labor Market
detail.abstract: Do firms voluntarily respond to local social issues? We explore this question through state-level hospital policies that promote breastfeeding. While these policies have a positive intergenerational impact on infants, they also create challenges for the female workforce, particularly new mothers. Although firms are not required to respond, some proactively adapt by creating a more parenting-friendly work environment. These improvements are concentrated in firms with greater female and minority representation on their boards and those with a high female labor dependency. While these voluntary efforts enhance employee satisfaction, they do not significantly affect firms' operating performance.

detail.title: Global Food Security Amid Geopolitical Tensions and Climate Risk : Trade Governance and Adaptive Strategies
detail.abstract: This work synthesizes evidence on how interacting geopolitical tensions and climate-related hazards shape food security across the dimensions of availability, access, utilization, and stability. It maps causal pathways by which extreme weather, shifting agroecological zones, soil and water degradation, and biodiversity loss combine with conflict, sanctions, export restrictions, and transport chokepoints to disrupt production, processing, and trade, generating price volatility and unequal impacts on vulnerable populations. Supply-chain concentration, limited storage, and damaged infrastructure amplify shocks, while displacement and labor losses weaken recovery prospects. Institutional capacity and policy choices determine whether early warnings, strategic reserves, social protection, and trade coordination translate into effective mitigation. A suite of adaptation and transformation options is evaluated, including climate-resilient varieties, precision and water-efficient farming, digital monitoring and forecast-based action, agroforestry and soil-carbon practices, circular economy measures, decentralized and urban food production, and nutrition-sensitive safety nets. Regional assessments illustrate heterogeneous exposure and response capacity across Africa, Asia, Latin America, Europe, and Oceania. Priorities for research and policy include modelling compound events, developing integrated socio-environmental scenarios, strengthening interdisciplinary decision support, and aligning finance and governance instruments to enable anticipatory, equitable interventions that sustain both nutrition and ecosystem services.

detail.abstract: Life expectancy has significantly increased in most parts of the world. The global life expectancy has increased by more than six years between 2000 and 2019, from 66.8 years to 73.4 years. Improving life expectancy and overall health has become an essential goal for the United Nations and numerous national governments from both developed and developing countries. This study examined the impact of economic growth on life expectancy in South Africa from 1994 to 2022. This study took a comprehensive approach by including control variables namely health expenditure, innovation and telecommunications. These variables were integrated into the analysis to provide a more thorough understanding of their potential influence on life expectancy in the nation. The investigation begins with a bounds testing of their potential influence on life expectancy, followed by the application of the ARDL (Autoregressive Distributed Lag) estimation technique. Additionally, the granger causality provides further insights into the temporal correlations among variables. The analysis reveals a noteworthy relationship between the variables in both short and long-term contexts, except GDP per capita, which proves insignificant in both the short and long run. As a result, the study highly recommends improving the efficiency and targeting of healthcare expenditure, aligning technological innovation with public health needs and using telecommunications strategically for healthcare outreach for South Africa to transition towards a healthier economy.

detail.title: Maintaining Empire: The Examination System and Secessionist Conflict in Imperial China
detail.abstract: The endurance of empire in China over much of the past two millennia contrasts starkly with the political fragmentation in Europe since the fall of Rome. To explain the persistence of China’s empire, we analyze the role of keju, the imperial civil service examination system. While geographic features and external threats impacted state formation, we argue that the systematic implementation of keju from the Song dynasty onward tied local elites to the imperial state, promoting centralized governance and reducing secessionist conflicts. Exploiting panel data spanning more than 4,200 grid cells and 20 centuries, we find robust evidence that areas producing more jinshi – the top exam passers – experienced significantly fewer secessionist wars. Our study shows how the examination system created the political incentives for imperial unity.

detail.abstract: This working paper advances the concept of Synthetica, the first AI-native cohort, building on work that maps generational identity to technological epochs rather than arbitrary birth years. Born from 2022 onward, Synthetica will grow up in environments mediated not by static media or algorithmic feeds but by adaptive AI companions, immersive mixed realities, autonomous systems, and-eventually-threshold brain-computer interfaces. The claim is political: whereas broadcast television shaped Baby Boomers and algorithmic platforms shaped Millennials and Gen Z, Synthetica's political life will be conditioned by synthetic infrastructures that mediate cognition, memory, and identity. Ownership and design of these systems amount to ownership of civic formation. The analysis synthesizes media theory, political communication, and developmental psychology to argue that democratic risks arise along four fronts: oligarchic capture, state-led cognitive control, invisible algorithmic gatekeeping, and adversarial misuse (deepfakes, cloning, and synthetic propaganda). Emerging debates over the moral status of advanced agents further escalate the constitutional stakes. The article situates Synthetica within the trajectory of media-politics relations and outlines a research agenda for safeguards for the synthetic age-cognitive sovereignty protections, transparency mandates, and democratic oversight of platform design. Outcomes are not foreordained: trajectories remain contingent on regulation, civic innovation, and public oversight.

detail.abstract: Tourism in Pacific Island economies, and the revenues derived from this sector, are heavily conditioned by the extreme geographic isolation of these states, the limited scale of their markets, and their reliance on air transport. This article examines air connectivity and transport costs as the principal determinants of tourism performance, drawing on a conceptual framework that integrates economic geography, development studies, and transport economics. The analysis does not rely exclusively on empirical estimation but instead situates Pacific Island economies within the broader literature on small states and peripheral markets, underscoring the structural constraints and opportunities arising from their spatial configuration. Evidence drawn from international aviation data, comparative case studies, and secondary sources suggests that air connectivity-measured in terms of network density, route diversity, and schedule reliability-acts as a catalyst for tourist inflows and revenue generation, while high transport costs remain a persistent impediment to market expansion. The study concludes that targeted aviation strategies, regional cooperation, and investment in resilient transport infrastructure are critical to supporting sustainable tourism-led growth in these economies.

detail.title: Research question: To what extent has the Rise of AI Disrupted Managerial Decision Making and Influenced Economic Productivity in Top Firms Globally?
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a revolutionary force in industries around the world, transforming managerial decision-making as well as reorganizing economic productivity. This essay examines to what degree AI has disturbed managerial routines and changed firm-level performance. Relying on secondary sources, case studies of successful companies like Amazon, Tesla, JPMorgan, and Unilever are considered. The findings indicate that AI has improved decision-making through the provision of data-led insights, predictive analytics, and operational effectiveness while, at the same time, introducing threats of algorithmic bias, overdependence on managers, and increasing gaps in productivity between leaders in AI adoption and laggards. The research findings conclude that even though AI has no doubt shaken up conventional managerial routines, its contribution to productivity is still unequal and contingent. The findings highlight that there is a call for equilibrium in which AI supports human decision-making, ethical principles direct the deployment of AI, and upskilling programs train managers to work in the AI era.

title: AI, Autonomy, and the New Security Dilemma: Deterrence, Escalation, and Strategic Ambiguity in the Algorithmic Age

detail.title: AI, Autonomy, and the New Security Dilemma: Deterrence, Escalation, and Strategic Ambiguity in the Algorithmic Age
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming the strategic landscape of international security by reshaping the foundational logic of deterrence, escalation, and ambiguity. This article examines how autonomous weapons and algorithmic decision-making challenge traditional deterrence theory, destabilize escalation pathways, and erode strategic signaling. Drawing on international relations theory and empirical case studies-including Israel's Harpy, Russia's Poseidon, and the U.S. Loyal Wingman-it analyzes how AI alters cost-benefit calculations, compresses decision cycles, and introduces interpretive opacity into conflict dynamics. The paper argues that AI systems complicate deterrence by undermining credibility and control, particularly in environments where decisions are made at machine speed and without human oversight. It explores the implications of black-box algorithms for strategic ambiguity and highlights the risks of inadvertent escalation through feedback loops and misclassification. Existing governance frameworks such as the CCW, UN GGE, and Tallinn Manual are shown to be inadequate for regulating autonomy, due to definitional ambiguity, verification challenges, and geopolitical asymmetries. To address these gaps, the article proposes policy interventions including algorithmic transparency, auditability, and AI-specific arms control. It calls for interdisciplinary collaboration and theoretical innovation to accommodate synthetic agency. As AI becomes central to military strategy, rethinking deterrence and governance is not optional-it is imperative for global stability.

title: How Well Are State-Dependent Local Projections Capturing the Nonlinearity?
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania

detail.title: How Well Are State-Dependent Local Projections Capturing the Nonlinearity?
detail.abstract: We evaluate how well state-dependent local projections recover true impulse responses in nonlinear environments. Using quadratic vector autoregressions as a laboratory, we show that linear local projections fail to capture any nonlinearities when shocks are symmetrically distributed. Popular state-dependent local projections specifications capture distinct aspects of nonlinearity: those interacting shocks with their signs capture higher-order effects, while those interacting shocks with lagged states capture state dependence. However, their gains over linear specifications arise primarily for extreme shocks or states. Our proposed specification—which augments the linear specification with a squared shock term and an interaction between the shock and lagged observables—best approximates the true responses across the entire joint distribution of shocks and states. An application to monetary policy reveals economically meaningful state dependence, whereas higher-order effects, though statistically significant, prove economically modest.

AI.tldr: 本文评估了状态依赖局部投影方法在非线性环境中恢复真实脉冲响应的能力。使用二次向量自回归作为实验平台，研究发现线性局部投影在对称分布冲击下无法捕捉非线性特征。流行的状态依赖局部投影规格分别捕捉非线性不同方面：冲击与符号交互捕捉高阶效应，冲击与滞后状态交互捕捉状态依赖。但相比线性规格的优势主要出现在极端冲击或状态时。作者提出的新规格（在线性规格基础上增加平方冲击项和冲击与滞后可观测变量交互项）在整个冲击和状态联合分布上最佳逼近真实响应。货币政策应用显示经济意义显著的状态依赖，而高阶效应虽统计显著但经济意义有限。

AI.method: 使用二次向量自回归作为实验平台，比较线性局部投影、不同状态依赖局部投影规格以及作者提出的新规格在恢复真实脉冲响应方面的表现

title: Resale Price Maintenance under Demand Uncertainty and Retail Competition *

detail.title: Resale Price Maintenance under Demand Uncertainty and Retail Competition *
detail.abstract: This paper extends the classic analysis of Deneckere et al. (1996, 1997) by examining how retailer competition shapes the effects of resale price maintenance (RPM) under demand uncertainty. In their framework, minimum RPM can benefit consumers by encouraging retailers to hold sufficient inventory, thereby lowering prices in high-demand states. We relax the assumption of perfect competition and analyze a continuum of downstream market structures, from monopoly to perfect competition. We show how the interaction of demand uncertainty and retail competition generates distinct regimes, and we identify the conditions under which RPM improves or harms consumer welfare. The results provide guidance for both antitrust policy and managerial strategy, highlighting that the pro-competitive effects of RPM are confined to industries with moderate demand uncertainty and intermediate levels of retail competition.

AI.tldr: 本文扩展了Deneckere等人的经典分析，研究零售商竞争如何在需求不确定性下影响转售价格维持（RPM）的效果。研究发现RPM的促进竞争效应仅限于具有适度需求不确定性和中等零售竞争水平的行业。
AI.research_question: 零售商竞争如何影响需求不确定性下转售价格维持（RPM）对消费者福利的影响？
AI.motivation: 扩展Deneckere等人的经典分析，放松完全竞争假设，分析从垄断到完全竞争的连续下游市场结构，探讨RPM在不同市场条件下的福利效应。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于Deneckere等人的RPM理论框架，结合需求不确定性和零售竞争理论，构建连续市场结构分析模型。
AI.method: 理论模型分析，通过放松完全竞争假设，分析从垄断到完全竞争的连续下游市场结构，识别不同参数条件下的福利效应。
AI.findings: RPM的促进竞争效应仅限于具有适度需求不确定性和中等零售竞争水平的行业；需求不确定性和零售竞争的相互作用会产生不同的制度效应。
AI.theory_contributions: 扩展了RPM理论框架，揭示了需求不确定性和零售竞争相互作用对RPM福利效应的影响机制。
AI.practical_contributions: 为反垄断政策和企业管理策略提供指导，帮助识别RPM可能产生促进竞争效应的行业条件。

title: The Implicit Costs of Biodiversity Conservation: Evidence from Corporate Investment Distortion in China
affiliations: Hunan University, Central South University, School of Economics, Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Hunan University

detail.title: The Implicit Costs of Biodiversity Conservation: Evidence from Corporate Investment Distortion in China
detail.abstract: We examine the implicit costs of biodiversity conservation mandates by exploiting the staggered rollout of China's Green Shield Action (GSA) as a quasi-natural experiment. A difference-indifferences analysis reveals that firms in affected cities reduce investment rates by 4.7 percentage points following GSA implementation. Two mechanisms drive this effect: (1) local governments facing fiscal pressure tighten tax enforcement and cut subsidies, reducing firm liquidity; and (2) increased operational uncertainty raises the value of delaying investment, consistent with real options theory. The effect is stronger for firms with irreversible capital, high competition, or elevated risk. We also find no evidence for a bank credit crowding-out effect and identify a significant slowdown in cross-regional investment into NNR cities by firms headquartered elsewhere. Our findings highlight a trade-off between ecological benefits and short-term economic costs, calling for complementary policies to align environmental and development goals.

title: Sanctions Evasion in the Russo-Ukrainian War: Challenges, Case Studies, and Policy Recommendations for the U.S. and EU

detail.title: Sanctions Evasion in the Russo-Ukrainian War: Challenges, Case Studies, and Policy Recommendations for the U.S. and EU

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the evasion of Western sanctions by Russia after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The central questions to the topic are how effectively Western sanctions have hindered Russia's war effort, what evasion tactics have emerged, and its significance to Western negotiation efforts to resolve the conflict. The paper begins with a holistic analysis of the sanctions themselves, dividing them into two categories: financial, and energy-related. It finds that while the measures have inflicted significant economic pain by isolating Russian banks, freezing over $300 billion in state assets, and cutting into energy revenues, Russia's economy has adapted using key evasion tactics. Through third-party countries, a "shadow fleet" of oil tankers, and alternative financial channels, Russia has managed to mitigate many of the sanctions' impacts. Case studies of China, India, Türkiye, and the UAE reveal exactly how partner nations have enabled this resilience. The paper then analyzes how these enforcement gaps will impact the geopolitics of peace negotiations, before considering crucial policy considerations from the perspectives of Western stakeholders. Finally, it concludes by providing policy recommendations for the U.S. and EU: expanding secondary sanctions, tightening loopholes in energy-related measures, establishing transatlantic unity, and developing a flexible sanctions framework. Ultimately, strengthening the credibility and impact of sanctions will be crucial in determining Western bargaining power when negotiating an eventual peace deal.

title: Household Debt and Women's Labor Supply: Evidence from India
affiliations: St Lawrence University

detail.title: Household Debt and Women's Labor Supply: Evidence from India
detail.abstract: I examine the effect of household debt and women's labor force participation in India. Using data from the 2011/12 India Human Development Survey, I employ a Two Stage Least Squares (TSLS) strategy to study the relationship. The percentage of neighboring households with debt within the primary sampling unit is used as an instrument to predict changes in household debt. 2nd stage results show that household debt significantly increases the likelihood of women's employment. This effect is particularly strong among women aged 36 to 45, those with limited or no schooling, and both high and low caste groups. I also find that household debt pushes women into agricultural and non-agricultural labor. Results are supported by several robustness checks including inverse probability weighting, biprobit estimation, and an alternative TSLS specification. Exclusion restriction is addressed by showing that the instrument does not predict changes in several household/primary sampling unit-level variables that can affect women's employment.

detail.title: Roots in Transition: Out-Migration Dynamics in North Bengal's Tea Gardens With Special Reference to Dheklapara and Bundapani Tea Gardens
detail.abstract: This study examines the out-migration dynamics of tea garden workers in North Bengal, with special reference to the Dheklapara and Bundapani estates. Since the liberalization of India’s economy, the closure and decline of several plantations have disrupted livelihoods, triggering large-scale migration. Drawing on fieldwork, interviews, and secondary data, the research analyzes the economic, political, and social factors shaping this process. It highlights how wage insecurity, shrinking welfare provisions, and the collapse of trade union influence have combined to push workers—particularly younger generations—toward urban centers and informal labor markets. The dissertation also explores the gendered dimensions of migration, showing how women face both vulnerability and new opportunities within this transition. By situating the North Bengal experience within broader debates on labor precarity and development, the study underscores how the tea garden crisis reflects wider patterns of marginalization in post-liberalization India. The findings suggest that meaningful policy intervention requires not only economic rehabilitation of plantations but also long-term social security and labor rights protections.

detail.abstract:
We analyzed written coverage positions for esketamine (Spravato) and other ketamine routes (IV, IM, oral) across Original Medicare (national program), all regional Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), and Medicare Advantage (MA) parent groups, enrollment-weighted to August 2025 (30,786,085 MA lives). 

As verified August 31, 2025, Original Medicare and every MAC publish no affirmative coverage policy ("Not Stated") despite existing HCPCS G-codes for Spravato visits (G2082, G2083). In MA, ~36.5% of enrollment (≈11.3M) is in plans that explicitly cover Spravato (~33.5% with prior authorization; ~3.1% without), while ~63.5% (≈19.5M) is "Not Stated." 

For non-Spravato routes, "Not Stated" predominates with notable explicit exclusions (especially IV). Implications for Medicare beneficiaries: policy silence in Original Medicare and MACs pushes claims into case-by-case review, making access contingent on documentation, local reviewer discretion, and persistence-slowing or blocking a fast-acting therapy for treatment-resistant depression. 

Implications for Medicare Advantage enrollees: only about one in three has a posted pathway (usually with prior authorization); for the majority under "Not Stated," plans typically default to non-coverage unless an exception is won. In practice, "Not Stated" functions as a barrier to transparency, increasing delays, denials, and abandonment risk. 

Conclusion: coverage clarity-not merely the existence of billing codes-governs real-world access; eliminating "Not Stated" and standardizing prior-authorization criteria would materially reduce inequities and time-to-first-dose.

AI.tldr: 该研究分析了美国医疗保险对艾氯胺酮（Spravato）和其他氯胺酮给药途径的覆盖政策，发现原始医疗保险和大多数地区承包商缺乏明确覆盖政策（"未说明"），导致患者获取治疗存在障碍。

AI.motivation: 了解医疗保险覆盖政策对快速起效的抗抑郁治疗（如艾氯胺酮）可及性的影响，揭示政策沉默如何成为治疗障碍。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于医疗政策分析框架，探讨保险覆盖透明度与患者治疗获取之间的关系。
AI.method: 分析原始医疗保险、地区医疗保险行政承包商和医疗保险优势计划的书面覆盖政策，采用2025年8月加权注册数据（30,786,085人）。

detail.abstract: This paper explores the application of three different portfolio formation rules using standard clustering techniques - K-means, K-mediods, and hierarchical - to a large financial data set (16 years of daily CRSP stock data) to determine how the choice of clustering technique may affect analysts' perceptions of the riskiness of different portfolios in the context of a prototype visual analytics system designed for financial stability monitoring. We use a two-phased experimental approach with visualizations to explore the effects of the different clustering techniques. The choice of clustering technique matters. There is significant variation among techniques, resulting in different "pictures" of the riskiness of the same underlying data when plotted to the visual analytics tool. This sensitivity to clustering methodology has the potential to mislead analysts about the riskiness of portfolios. We conclude that further research into the implications of portfolio formation rules is needed, and that visual analytics tools should not limit analysts to a single clustering technique, but instead should provide the facility to explore the data using different techniques.

AI.method: 采用两阶段实验方法，将三种聚类技术（K-means、K-mediods、层次聚类）应用于16年每日CRSP股票数据，通过可视化分析工具比较不同技术产生的风险性评估结果。

detail.abstract: Poland opted for a broad-scale endorsement of the Nutri-Score at a time when its perception has become increasingly more critical. The first companies, due to changes in the Nutri-Score's algorithm, already abandoned it, arguing that different treatments of food items depending on the way they are consumed would rather confuse consumers than continue its signaling function. The two joint choice experiments, using drinking and eating yogurts as example stimuli, are conducted with Polish consumers. Results indicate that among them, the Nutri-Score fulfills its signaling function well, whereas it is primarily the extreme ratings that attract or deter consumers. Thus, its replacement by a simpler label like Sweden's Keyhole label is discussed. The results furthermore indicate that neither the willingness to purchase a product nor its perceived healthiness are impacted by the type of yogurt, but the effect strength of the Nutri-Score’s signaling function is. Consequently, the Nutri-Score functions differently for different types of food items, and even small differences as between an exemplary drinking and eating yogurt might affect its effectiveness. Consequently, the Polish government made the right choice in adopting the Nutri-Score in the context of its nutrition policy, but it should study further whether simpler labels may fulfill the same function. Since consumer behavior differs with product type, the Nutri-Score committee is advised to rather focus their efforts on integrating actual consumer behavior in the Nutri-Score algorithm than the way it is consumed.

AI.method: 两个联合选择实验，以饮用型和食用型酸奶作为刺激物，针对波兰消费者进行测试
AI.findings: 1) Nutri-Score在波兰消费者中能良好发挥信号功能；2) 主要是极端评级吸引或阻止消费者；3) 产品购买意愿和感知健康度不受酸奶类型影响，但Nutri-Score信号功能的效果强度受影响；4) Nutri-Score对不同食品类型作用不同
AI.theory_contributions: 揭示了食品标签效果的产品类型依赖性，为营养标签理论提供了实证支持，强调了消费者行为在标签设计中的重要性

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the European Central Bank’s Multi Country model (ECB-MC), a coherent macroeconomic framework designed to support economic forecasting and policy analysis within the Eurosystem. The ECB-MC captures the economic dynamics of the five major economies in the euro area – Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and the Netherlands – which account for more than 80 percent of the euro area total GDP. By incorporating detailed structural features and data-driven insights, the model provides the main reference for the ECB’s staff macroeconomic projections, acting as a disciplined tool for forecasting, enabling scenario, risk and sensitivity analyses, and giving a framework to understand the transmission channels of various economic shocks. The paper offers a detailed account of the structure, the estimation and the model properties, and provides a primer on the potential uses of the ECB-MC in the Eurosystem macroeconomic projections.

detail.title: Rising Energy Prices Without Falling Consumption? The Role of Energy Price Dispersion in a Multi-Product World

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZEW - Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper No. 25-047
publicationDetails.journalName: ZEW - Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Governments around the world are under pressure to reduce industrial energy use and emissions without losing out to international competition. For this reason, climate policies often come with exemptions or additional support for large energyintensive firms, increasing the heterogeneity in energy prices. We document such a rising dispersion in industrial energy prices in the German manufacturing sector that coincides with rising average energy prices. Surprisingly, we observe an increase in industrial energy intensity, while at the same time, manufacturing firms have shifted toward producing less energy intensive products. We develop a model of multi-product firms with heterogeneous energy prices and heterogeneous products that can partially explain this puzzle via a 'reshuffling' among producers: If energy prices rise only for a share of firms, those firms will drop energy-intensive products. But the remaining low energy price firms will increase their market share of these products and produce them in a less energy-efficient way. Empirical analyses based on German administrative firm data suggest that such a 'reshuffling' is indeed taking place. We show in a simple quantification that reshuffling can have sizable effects on aggregate energy intensity.

AI.tldr: 本文研究了德国制造业中能源价格分散化对能源强度的影响，发现虽然平均能源价格上涨，但工业能源强度反而增加。通过多产品企业模型，揭示了企业间产品重组机制：高能源价格企业放弃能源密集型产品，而低能源价格企业增加这些产品的市场份额并以较低能效生产。
AI.research_question: 为什么在德国制造业中，随着能源价格上涨和分散化，工业能源强度反而增加？
AI.motivation: 各国政府在减少工业能源使用和排放的同时面临国际竞争压力，导致气候政策对大型能源密集型企业提供豁免或额外支持，增加了能源价格的异质性。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于多产品企业模型，考虑企业间能源价格异质性和产品异质性，分析产品重组对能源强度的影响。
AI.method: 使用德国行政企业数据进行实证分析，结合理论模型和简单量化分析。
AI.findings: 实证证据支持产品重组机制的存在：高能源价格企业放弃能源密集型产品，低能源价格企业增加这些产品的市场份额并以较低能效生产，导致总体能源强度上升。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了能源价格分散化背景下企业产品重组的新机制，解释了能源强度与能源价格关系的反常现象。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者提供了重要启示：单纯提高平均能源价格可能因企业间重组效应而无法有效降低总体能源强度，需要考虑政策设计的公平性和全面性。

detail.abstract: This paper examines the degree of persistence of China’s travel “credit” and “debt” series in the balance of payments. This is an important issue because the travel component in the balance of payments of travel is one of the main indicators measuring the contribution of tourism to a country’s economic activity, and knowledge of its persistence is critical to assess the potential impact of disrupting factors such as the COVID-19 pandemic. The analysis is carried out using a fractional integration framework, which provides evidence of mean reversion in the credit series, but not in the debt series. The policy implications of these findings are also discussed.

title: Lack of Access to Drinking Water on Household Premises and Educational Outcomes of Children in Rural India
affiliations: and The University of Manchester

detail.title: Lack of Access to Drinking Water on Household Premises and Educational Outcomes of Children in Rural India

keywords: Instrumental Variables JEL classification codes: Q25

detail.abstract: Access to drinking water on household premises is a basic necessity with significant implications for children's educational outcomes. In many parts of rural India, where water collection demands considerable time and effort, especially from women and girls, the lack of on-premises access can disrupt daily routines and hinder educational engagement. To shed light on the same, this study examines the relationship between the lack of access to drinking water on household premises and educational outcomes among rural children aged 12-18, focusing on school attendance, years of schooling, and age-appropriate grade progression. Utilising data from Phase 1 states and union territories (UTs) of the 5th round of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), we find that children in households without drinking water on the premises have poorer outcomes across all three educational measures. These findings remain robust across alternative estimation methods, the inclusion of data from NFHS-4, and complementary educational indicators drawn from the 2019 Time Use Survey (TUS). The adverse effects are especially pronounced for females, partly due to their disproportionate involvement in water-fetching responsibilities. Given the critical role of education in shaping long-term well-being, these findings carry important policy implications for rural India, where secondary school completion rates remain low and learning gaps persist.

title: Optimal Stopping Time Strategy for Paying Tax
affiliations: , ESPRIT School of Engineering and Asia University, Department of Finance

detail.title: Optimal Stopping Time Strategy for Paying Tax
detail.abstract: Purpose: In this study, we examine the strategic timing for paying corporate taxes under varying financial market conditions. Design/methodology/approach: We develop a model by using optimal stopping theory and considering three tax regimes: (i) no tax, the firm is never required to pay taxes; (ii) paid tax on a monthly basis, taxes paid based on revenues periodically; and (iii) deferred tax with penalties, delaying taxes but incurring financial penalties. Findings: Our results indicate that the optimal timing of tax payments is highly sensitive to market parameters such as drift, volatility, and the structure of tax penalties. The evidence further suggests that, under certain risk conditions, tax deferral can serve as a legitimate and value-enhancing strategy, allowing firms to retain more earnings and allocate resources more efficiently. Originality: Our main contribution is to identify how timing strategies are shaped by drift, volatility, and tax penalties. The model is developed theoretically and supported by a Monte Carlo simulation. We also address the legal and policy implications of tax deferral, namely that under certain risk conditions, tax deferral increases firm value. Overall, our conclusions are based on mathematically rigorous modeling and simulations.

AI.tldr: 本研究通过最优停止理论模型探讨企业在不同金融市场条件下的最优纳税时机策略，发现纳税时机对市场参数（漂移率、波动率）和税收惩罚结构高度敏感，在特定风险条件下税收递延可成为价值增值策略。

title: Social Finance in the Age of AI: A Tale of Two Platforms

detail.title: Social Finance in the Age of AI: A Tale of Two Platforms
detail.abstract: This paper studies how investors use generative AI in discussions across two major investing social media platforms with distinct governance and user bases: Seeking Alpha and Reddit's r/WallStreetBets. We document sharp cross-platform differences in adoption and market outcomes. On Seeking Alpha, AI adoption arises when information is scarce or contributors cover unfamiliar stocks; it is associated with more informative retail order flows, reduced user disagreement, and narrower bid-ask spreads. On WallStreetBets, AI adoption rises following surges in retail buying and is linked to sentiment contagion. Adoption is also followed by higher abnormal trading volume and volatility, wider spreads, and lottery-like return distributions. These results indicate that the adoption of AI and its relation to market outcomes are shaped by the institutional and behavioral context in which it is deployed.

title: The Cowichan Case: Aboriginal Title in Common Law Countries
affiliations: Harvard University - Harvard Law School

detail.title: The Cowichan Case: Aboriginal Title in Common Law Countries
detail.abstract: Canada is not typically known within the common law system for landmark precedents. Nonetheless, Aboriginal and indigenous law has been one area in which Canada has long had a progressive and “enlightened” reputation compared to other common law countries. Most recently, in August 2025, the British Columbia Supreme Court made a groundbreaking decision in Cowichan Tribes v Canada (Attorney General), which ruled that the government’s transfer of property rights to private entities over Aboriginal lands infringed on Aboriginal title. In other words, if the ruling is upheld, then the Canadian land title system is now burdened by or is subject to the Aboriginal title system. However, since any final decision from the Supreme Court of Canada on the case is likely to be years away, it may be worthwhile at this time to analyze this groundbreaking decision at length to understand the ramifications if any of the decision from the perspective of comparative indigenous law. In this way, the differences between the Aboriginal title systems of other common law countries and jurisdictions can be assessed as well.

detail.abstract: This article examines the role of tourism as a catalyst for economic convergence between small island economies and the global economy. Small island states often face structural constraints such as geographic isolation, limited natural resources, and high vulnerability to external shocks. However, tourism provides an opportunity to integrate into international trade networks, attract foreign direct investment, and diversify income sources. Drawing on empirical evidence and comparative case studies, the study highlights how tourism fosters knowledge transfer, infrastructure development, and labor mobility, thereby narrowing developmental gaps. At the same time, the paper addresses the risks of overdependence on tourism, including environmental degradation, socio-cultural pressures, and exposure to global market fluctuations. The findings suggest that sustainable tourism strategies, embedded within broader economic policy frameworks, are essential for ensuring long-term convergence and resilience in small island economies.

detail.abstract: Close examination of the American consumer market will identify a highly competitive market with strong product differentiation, where each product is of limited production volume. In addition, there is also a strong and varied price signal in operation to distribute these varied products of limited stock. Theoretically, slight differentiation in product specification should lead to slight price difference. This then exerts a price signal to influence the number of units sold. Compare this to an economy that pursues mass production of a few product models. Here the product differentiation is not fine grained, but of marked difference between models in the range of 50 to 250 dollars. Hence, the price signal is also not strong as the high price and low price items have their own stable consumer groups. Overall, in economies with strong product competition, varied product differentiation will emerge, and the price signal is also varied and strong to help distribute the limited stock to the willing buyer.

detail.title: Environmental Summits and Innovation
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of Conference of the Parties (COP) summits on innovation using an event study framework. Innovation is measured by patent grants, distinguishing between the total number of patents and the number of patents in environmental technologies, based on the World Intellectual Property Organization classification. We find that hosting a COP summit leads to a significant and lasting increase in the total number of patent grants, with an average rise of about 35 percent per year from the seventh to the thirteenth year after the summit, but has only a limited effect on the number of patent grants in environmental technologies. We further examine potential heterogeneity in the effects of COP summits by analyzing the impact of hosting a summit on patents in environmental technology compared to other technologies separately for each host country. The results suggest that while hosting a COP summit generally promotes environmental patenting, the effect is negative in some countries. We discuss possible reasons, including diminishing returns in green innovation and the influence of large industrial emitters. The findings are robust across alternative estimators, the inclusion of control variables, and different measures of patenting activity.

title: Convergence of Blockchain, AI, and Quantum Computing in FinTech

detail.title: Convergence of Blockchain, AI, and Quantum Computing in FinTech
detail.abstract: The financial sector is witnessing a paradigm shift driven by the convergence of distributed ledger technology, machine learning and nascent quantum computing techniques. While each technology has attracted independent academic and commercial interest, their combined application in fixed income markets promises to transform issuance, settlement and risk management. This study synthesizes public case-studies and regulatory initiatives to map this convergence. First, we examine tokenised debt issuances such as the World Bank's bond-i and accelerated settlement projects like the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation's Project Ion. Second, we review emerging guidelines for trustworthy artificial intelligence, including the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology's (NIST) Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework, and discuss regulatory expectations for explainable credit decisions. Third, we analyse the potential of quantum algorithms for portfolio optimisation and the parallel push for post-quantum cryptography, such as NIST's August 2024 standards ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA. Our analysis highlights synergies between these domains-blockchain offers immutable datasets for AI models, AI improves decision making on tokenised instruments, and quantum computing accelerates optimisation-but also underscores risks ranging from biased algorithms to cryptographic obsolescence. We propose that integrated governance frameworks and early adoption of post-quantum standards are essential to harness these opportunities responsibly.

detail.title: Against Trade Secrets Protection for "Semi-public" Databases

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in the Singapore Journal of Legal Studies

detail.abstract: This article examines whether trade secrets law should be applied to protect "semi-public" databases with frontend data access that is open to the public. It argues that the incentive-based justification, whether grounded in the traditional rationale or reframed through an investment lens, does not provide a compelling basis for extending protection. The business efficiency rationale may arguably support trade secrets protection only where frontend access is restricted to a clearly defined and limited group of users. By contrast, when access is open to an indefinite public, ambiguous legal standards fail to mitigate inefficiencies and may even intensify the technological arms race between data holders and scrapers. Although deterrence could, theoretically, yield efficiency benefits, such an effect rests on a flawed assumption and risks suppressing activities that serve the public interest. Moreover, given the already powerful and arguably overprotective alternatives available to database holders, introducing trade secrets protection in this context risks further distorting the balance between private and public interests.

detail.title: Aim High or Play Safe? Commitment, Prosocial Incentives, and Goal Setting
detail.abstract: We examine how behavioral incentives affect goal setting and performance when individuals choose their own goals. Using a model with reference-dependent preferences and effort cost uncertainty, we predict that commitment mechanisms improve performance by inducing more conservative goal selection to increase attainability, while prosocial incentives enhance performance by preserving ambitious goals and increasing motivation. Two preregistered experiments confirm these predictions. In an online real-effort task, soft commitment reduced goals relative to controls but significantly increased performance, while prosocial incentives (charitable donations contingent on goal achievement) maintained goal levels and generated even greater performance gains. A field experiment lasting 4 weeks with students setting daily exercise goals yields similar results: commitment lowered goals while significantly increasing performance, while prosocial incentives preserved ambitious targets and delivered the strongest performance improvements that persisted throughout the duration of the experiment. The mechanisms differ: commitment operates through enhanced goal attainability, while prosocial incentives work by sustaining both ambitious targets and intrinsic motivation. These findings inform the design of performance contracts and suggest that prosocial framing may dominate punitive commitment mechanisms in uncertain environments.

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animals; therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received to assist with the preparation of this manuscript.

detail.abstract: This study looks at how international tax rules work to control cryptocurrency transactions. It is based on IFRS rules and the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). The researcher uses a new global dataset covering the years 2011 to 2025. The study introduces ten measures: the Global Regulatory Coverage Index (GRCI), the Global IFRS Alignment Score (GIFRSAS), the Global Tax Compliance Effectiveness Score (GTCES), the Global Cross-Border Arbitrage Index (GCBAI), the Global Disclosure Quality Index (GDQI), the Global Enforcement Capacity Score (GECS), the Global Detection Rate (GDR), the Global Penalty Collection Ratio (GPCR), the Global Convergence Score (GCS), and the Global Policy Diffusion Speed (GPDS). These measures show both how much regulation is in place and how well people follow the rules. The study uses several methods, including describing data, looking at how variables are connected, and using time-based analysis to understand how these factors relate to each other. The results show a strong link between how much regulation is in place and cross-border arbitrage, with a correlation of-0.97. This means that when more countries follow CARF and IFRS reporting, there is less chance of people taking advantage of tax differences in different countries. The study shows that working together internationally, spreading new rules quickly, and having strong enforcement are all important for tax compliance and reducing arbitrage. The study adds value by offering an easy-to-use framework, new measures, and important evidence for policymakers. It concludes that international tax changes can help with compliance and reduce arbitrage only when regulation, IFRS alignment, and enforcement all improve at the same time.

detail.abstract: The global aid architecture-often described as the "Aid Industrial Complex" (AIC)-continues to struggle with shifting power and resources to communities. Independent analyses indicate that a small share of humanitarian funding reaches local and national actors directly, with recent estimates of ~0.6% of first disbursements (and ~4-6% when certain indirect flows are included, though figures vary by source and methodology). This article advances science diplomacy-the strategic use of scientific cooperation to build trust, inform policy, and bridge geopolitical divides-as a practical pathway to unwind AIC hierarchies and establish equitable, co-governed partnerships. Grounded in dependency theory, postcolonial critique, and complex adaptive systems (CAS), the study synthesizes more than 120 sources (2016-September 2025) and develops a four-pillar framework spanning: (1) trust-building research alliances that institutionalize local leadership and integrate traditional ecological knowledge; (2) geopolitical bridge-building through neutral, evidence-based platforms; (3) technology and data diplomacy enabling responsible AI and open, FAIR data sharing; and (4) institutional reforms that hard-wire inclusion, open science, and verifiable localization. Evidence drawn from the Ebola response, PEPFAR, SESAME, UNESCO's FRIEND-Nile, and disruptions to Arctic research demonstrates where science diplomacy has delivered durable collaboration-and where it has been constrained by protectionism, elite capture, gender inequities, and epistemic exclusion. The article concludes with a timed policy agenda specifying actions for donors, governments, and NGOs to embed science-diplomacy mechanisms that redirect resources, decision rights, and accountability toward communities. While ambitious, the agenda acknowledges political and fiscal constraints and frames recommendations as direction-setting benchmarks rather than rigid forecasts.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether firm-specific cyclical and idiosyncratic risk profiles influence corporate bond spreads and the transmission of monetary policy. I extend the standard excess bond premium (EBP) framework of Gilchrist & Zakrajšek (2012) to allow investors’ required compensation for default risk to vary with firm-level risks. Incorporating these effects reveals that a significantly larger share of a monetary policy shock’s impact on credit spreads is driven by changes in default risk compensation (as opposed to the EBP). In particular, for firms with more cyclical risk, up to one-fourth of the additional spread widening following a contractionary monetary policy shock reflects higher expected default compensation, substantially more than implied by the traditional EBP. By contrast, firms with high idiosyncratic risk show no strong differential response to monetary policy shocks relative to other firms.

detail.abstract: This study critically examines Jordan's exchange rate policy, which has been anchored to the U.S. dollar since 1995, amid shifting global economic dynamics and increasing trade diversification. The primary aim is to assess the necessity and implications of transitioning from a fixed dollar peg to a more adaptive currency basket arrangement. Key research questions focus on identifying the factors driving the need for this transition, evaluating how a calibrated currency basket could enhance Jordan's resilience and competitiveness in international markets, and analyzing the influence of the EU-Jordan Strategic Partnership on monetary policy decisions. The findings indicate that while the dollar peg has provided short-term stability, it increasingly restricts Jordan's monetary policy autonomy and exposes the economy to external shocks, particularly from the U.S. economy. The research reveals that a diversified currency basket, reflecting trade patterns with the EU, GCC, and Asian markets, could mitigate these vulnerabilities and support deeper economic integration. The paper argues that adopting a basket arrangement aligns Jordan's monetary policy with its evolving economic realities, ensuring better adaptability to global market fluctuations.The overall conclusion is a transparent, rule-based currency basket that encompasses the U.S. dollar, euro, and regional currencies, enabling Jordan to enhance its macroeconomic resilience while fostering sustainable growth. The proposed framework not only reflects Jordan's unique economic structure but also serves as a potential model for other emerging economies facing similar challenges in a rapidly changing global landscape.

detail.title: Balancing Investor Rights and State Regulatory Sovereignty in India's Bilateral Investment Treaties
detail.abstract: The interplay between securing investor rights and upholding state regulatory authority is a pivotal area of focus within international economic law. India's engagement with Bilateral Investment Treaties (BITs) since the early 1990s has significantly shaped its foreign investment regulatory framework. Yet, this involvement has underscored profound tensions, as exemplified by landmark cases such as Vodafone v. Union of India, where the dichotomy between investor protections and sovereign autonomy is starkly evident. Central to this discourse is the revised 2016 Model BIT, implemented following adverse outcomes in international arbitrations like the case against White Industries Australia Limited. This study critically examines the provisions of the 2016 Model BIT, aimed at rebalancing investor protection with state regulatory powers. Through detailed analysis, the paper identifies challenges in achieving a fair distribution of rights and responsibilities. Additionally, this paper evaluates the EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) as a model that successfully balances investor rights with state regulatory interests. It argues for a refined treaty drafting approach, inspired by CETA's provisions, that effectively addresses the complexities of global investments while ensuring that BITs support equitable investment practices without compromising the regulatory mandates of the host state. This research contributes to the broader discussion on optimizing BIT frameworks to better serve national and international investment objectives, offering strategic insights for emerging economies navigating global investment treaty landscapes.

detail.abstract: We study sequential auctions for allocating multiple heterogeneous objects with mixed differentiation to unit-demand agents. Objects can be divided into two groups: in one, valuations are strictly increasing in type; in the other, strictly decreasing. If within each group the objects can be ordered in decreasing variation of values, then any combination of static standard auctions implemented in this sequence achieves full efficiency. Moreover, the principal's expected revenue equals the sum of the constrained optimal revenues for the two groups. These results highlight the advantage of sequential auctions (over simultaneous auctions) in achieving efficiency while still generating reasonable revenue.

detail.abstract: This study examines the causal effects of the ACA’s health insurance reforms on labor market extensive and intensive margins among pre-retirees, focusing on a racial disparity. Using double robust method of Propensity Score Matching with ATT and a Staggered Difference in Differences, we estimate the impact of Health Insurance Marketplace Subsidies (HIMS) and Medicaid expansion. Our findings indicate that HIMS delays retirement and prevents labor force exit with Number Needed to Treat (NNT) = 132, meaning for every 132 individuals subsidized, one additional person stays employed who would have otherwise exited. On the intensive margin, HIMS increases part-time work by 1.51 percentage points (NNT = 66). Weekly hours drop by 1.24. Racial disparities emerge, with White and Other racial groups (Asians) benefiting most, while Black and Hispanic workers experience weaker effects. No significant labor market effect are observed from Medicaid expansion.

detail.abstract:
We reviewed official Medicaid coverage documents from 165 policy-making entities across 51 U.S. jurisdictions (state agencies, MCOs, and PBM carve-outs) captured in August 2025.

Esketamine (Spravato) is covered by 75/165 entities (45.5%; 72/75 with prior authorization), while 90/165 (54.5%) are Not Stated; alternative ketamine routes are effectively unavailable (IV 1/165 [0.6%], IM 0, oral largely Not Stated), and six jurisdictions have no covering entities.

Objective: Quantify real-world Medicaid access to ketamine therapies by comparing coverage decisions across all policy-making entities inside each state. 

Findings: Coverage for esketamine (Spravato) appears in 75 of 165 entities (45.5%); 90 of 165 (54.5%) are Not Stated. Among covering entities, 72 of 75 (96%) require prior authorization. Six jurisdictions have no covering entities at all. Because MCOs control 100 of 165 decision points (60.6%), intrastate inconsistencies are common-states may publish a policy that covers Spravato while one or more in-state MCOs do not-creating confusion and unequal access based on plan assignment. 

Alternative routes used for treatment-resistant depression are effectively unavailable: IV is covered by 1 of 165 entities (0.6%), IM by 0, and oral is largely Not Stated. Net effect: 98.2% of entities require some form of individual review before treatment proceeds. 

Methods: Cross-sectional review of publicly posted Medicaid coverage documents (PDF/HTML) from state Medicaid agencies, managed care organizations (MCOs), and pharmacy/PBM carve-outs across 51 jurisdictions. Data were captured in August 2025 from official domains only; route-specific determinations were coded and tallied at the entity level. Conclusion: Nominal coverage does not reliably translate into timely care. 

Policy silence and near-universal prior authorization produce predictable delays-and, where state and MCO policies conflict, unequal access for beneficiaries in the same state. The paper closes with actionable fixes: uniform criteria, expedited pathways for psychiatric crises, and basic transparency requirements to turn paper coverage into real-world treatment.

detail.title: Household Discount Rate Heterogeneity and Policy Transmission
detail.abstract: Discount rates are central to households' investment, consumptions and savings choices, and are a key determinant of aggregate spending and growth. We develop an empirical menu approach to identifying individual's discount rates. In making credit choices, consumers are often faced with decisions consisting of maturity and interest rate choices. We show that using the structure of consumers' preferences, consumers' maturity choices are informative about their discount rates as more patient consumers pick longer-maturities with more favorable rates. We estimate discount rates using a financial choice which trades-off smaller cashflows in the short term against larger cash flows in the future-the choice of bank time deposits and 182,540 term choices made by 46,746 account holders at a large Indian bank. We estimate an average discount rate of 11.6% and exhibit significant heterogeneity. Estimated discount rate predict savings and portfolio choices, as well as stock market participation. Discount rates rise during economic contractions, consistent with Keynesian theory. Individuals with higher discount rates invest more in equities following monetary policy loosening, suggesting that discount rate heterogeneity can play a role in monetary policy passthrough.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a simple methodology for using artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots in the policy modelling. We outline, step by step, how to systematically proposing a methodology the support of AI chatbot such as ChatGPT. This new methodology, called Artificial Intelligence Policy Modelling (AIPM), offers a transformative approach to teaching, learning, and researching policy modelling from a methodological perspective. detail.abstract: This paper presents a thought experiment utilizing a large language model (DeepSeek-v3) to simulate a full academic peer-review process for a hypothetical proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. We task the AI to first generate a novel, interdisciplinary proof strategy involving the Fargues-Fontaine curve, Shimura varieties, and a twisted Dirac operator. Subsequently, we prompt the AI to adopt the personas of critical peer reviewers to analyze the proposed proof. The simulation results in a rigorous critique, identifying fatal flaws such as undefined central objects and circular logic. Notably, the AI then synthesizes this criticism to reframe the failed proof into a credible long-term research program. This exercise demonstrates the potential of AI as a tool for conceptual stress-testing and generating academically rigorous discourse within scientific research.

detail.title: General Social Agents
detail.abstract: Useful social science theories predict behavior across settings. However, applying a theory to make predictions in new settings is challenging: rarely can it be done without ad hoc modifications to account for setting-specific factors. We argue that AI agents put in simulations of those novel settings offer an alternative for applying theory, requiring minimal or no modifications. We present an approach for building such "general" agents that use theory-grounded natural language instructions, existing empirical data, and knowledge acquired by the underlying AI during training. To demonstrate the approach in settings where no data from that data-generating process exists-as is often the case in applied prediction problems-we design a heterogeneous population of 883,320 novel games. AI agents are constructed using human data from a small set of conceptually related but structurally distinct "seed" games. In preregistered experiments, on average, agents predict initial human play in a random sample of 1,500 games from the population better than (i) a cognitive hierarchy model, (ii) game-theoretic equilibria, and (iii) out-of-the-box agents. For a small set of separate novel games, these simulations predict responses from a new sample of human subjects better even than the most plausibly relevant published human data.
