detail.abstract: This paper analyzes bank lending behavior toward novel clean energy technologies in the presence of high screening costs and potential learning-by-lending. In a two-period model, bank loans in the first period build up banks' financing experience with the novel technology, which improves lending profitability and partially spills over to peers. Because of these learning externalities, such early-stage loans are either undersupplied by the market (a cooperation problem) or do not occur at all if the banking sector remains stuck in an inferior market equilibrium with no lending (a coordination problem). We propose a policy mix in which public loan provision eliminates the inferior equilibrium, thereby resolving the coordination problem, while de-risking subsidies internalize learning spillovers to peers. Our findings highlight the role of public financial policies if environmental and innovation externalities are already addressed, and we provide a numerical application to the early stage of offshore wind energy in Germany as a plausible context for our policy implications.

detail.title: A Comparative Study Of International Best Practices Employed In Striking A Balance Between The Functionality Of Competition Law And Protection Of Ip Rights As They Operate Within The Marketplace
detail.abstract:
The contemporary global economy is fundamentally shaped by the intricate yet subtle relationship between IP rights and competition law. These two legal disciplines may seem to have different goals at first, but they are actually two sides of the same coin that drive innovation and economic growth.

Intellectual property, which includes patents, copyrights, and trademarks, gives creators and innovators exclusive rights. These exclusive rights create limited monopolies designed to incentivise research, development, and creative output. On the other hand, competition law, also known as antitrust law, tries to stop monopolistic abuses and anti-competitive practices. It does this by making sure that the market is fair for all competitors, encouraging lower prices, and giving consumers more options.

The main goal of both IP rights and competition law is to improve consumer welfare and boost economic growth. But in practice, the exclusive rights that come with IP rights can give certain market players a lot of market power, which can lead to higher prices and make it harder for new competitors to enter the market. The challenge for legal authorities is managing the delicate balance between enforcing IP rights and ensuring fair competition.

This paper undertakes to carry out a comparative study of international best practices in striking this crucial balance. The goal of this research is to show how important this issue is to Uganda as a developing economy and to identify which international best practices may be adopted and effectively applied to the Ugandan context.

title: Joint Forest Management in Meghalaya: A Study of Community Development and Participation

detail.title: Joint Forest Management in Meghalaya: A Study of Community Development and Participation
detail.abstract: Human life depends on forests, which are essential natural resources, especially for the communities that live there and nearby. Numerous plant and animal species act as a haven for biodiversity by providing resources like non timber forest products, herbs, and other resources for clothing and shelter; this abundant biodiversity makes ecosystems more resilient and sustains livelihoods. Joint Forest Management (JFM) contributes significantly to forest protection and community welfare by engaging the local people in safeguarding and managing the forest resources. Joint Forest Management (JFM) in Meghalaya is an important model of communitybased forest management that incorporates traditional ecological wisdom and state-initiated conservation programs. Forests play a critical role in maintaining livelihoods, cultural heritage, and biodiversity, particularly among indigenous groups. This paper examines the operation and impacts of Joint Forest Management (JFM) in Nongwah village, East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya. Drawing from field observations and village narratives, it examines roles and duties undertaken by community agents, impacts of community-managed afforestation, and socioeconomic benefits derived from infrastructure development linked to JFM. With this research, the literature is enriched with recording the interface of customary and formal institutions of forest governance. In the process, it addresses an essential lacuna in the forest policy literature in northeast India.

title: A Global Test for Systematic Superiority
affiliations: University of Agder - School of Business and Law

detail.title: A Global Test for Systematic Superiority
detail.abstract: We propose a statistical test for the global hypothesis that a strategy systematically outperforms its benchmark across multiple datasets. Traditional approaches rely on individual p-values, which permit only sample-specific statements and cannot establish systematic superiority. Our method aggregates evidence using a multivariate stationary block bootstrap that preserves both time-series and cross-sectional dependence, providing valid inference for a global test. The procedure directly addresses the challenge of distinguishing systematic improvements from chance findings or isolated successes. Although we illustrate the method in an investment setting, its scope is much broader. The test can be applied to evaluate collections of trading rules, the average performance of portfolio managers, the robustness of asset-pricing anomalies, or the reliability of forecasting and risk management models. By moving beyond isolated p-values, the framework offers a principled approach to inference on global superiority.

title: Family Planning, Institutional Change, and Missing Girls
affiliations: Xiamen University - School of Economics and Xiamen University - School of Economics

detail.title: Family Planning, Institutional Change, and Missing Girls
detail.abstract: China faces one of the world's most severe missing girls problems. The literature largely attributes this phenomenon to the country's family planning policy. However, whether that policy actually produced missing girls may have depended on the economic system, which underwent a major shift with the introduction of the household responsibility system (HRS). Using census data, we find that stricter birth quotas before the HRS did not lead to missing girls. Only after the adoption of the HRS did stricter quota significantly increase the probability that families with a firstborn girl would have a boy at the next birth. Under the HRS, the abandonment of girls was the primary method of sex selection in response to one-child policy. The likely channel through which the HRS enabled sex selection was its weakening of the state's capacity to penalize sex-selective practices.

title: Fertile Ground or Barren Policy? Evaluating Cross-Convention Approaches to Soil Protection

detail.title: Fertile Ground or Barren Policy? Evaluating Cross-Convention Approaches to Soil Protection

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in International Yearbook of Soil Law and Policy 2025

detail.abstract: Soils are increasingly recognised as a cornerstone of sustainable development, climate resilience, and biodiversity conservation. They serve as the foundation for terrestrial ecosystems, agricultural productivity, and the regulation of global biogeochemical cycles. Yet, in international environmental law, soils remain conceptually marginal and institutionally fragmented. No dedicated treaty or comprehensive legal regime exists to protect or govern soils holistically. Instead, soils are addressed indirectly and unevenly across a patchwork of multilateral environmental agreements-most notably, the three Rio Conventions adopted in the wake of the 1992 Earth Summit: the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), and the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). This chapter explores the evolving treatment of soils across these three Conventions, with a focus on the outcomes of the 2024-2025 Conferences of the Parties (COPs). It examines the extent to which soil-related objectives are being integrated across the climate, biodiversity, and land degradation agendas, drawing on the normative framing of the 2024 United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA-6) Resolution 6/14 and the Pact for the Future adopted by the UN General Assembly. In so doing, the chapter identifies emerging synergies, persistent gaps, and potential legal entry points for greater cross-regime coherence. Rather than offering prescriptive recommendations, the chapter adopts a descriptive-analytical approach to assess institutional dynamics and legal language. It argues that while high-level aspirations around land restoration and soil health have gained momentum, the operationalisation of these goals remains uneven. Institutional integration across the Rio Conventions is still largely superficial, constrained by distinct mandates, differing legal architectures, and a lack of common monitoring frameworks. Nevertheless, soils present a compelling site for rethinking interlinkages across environmental regimes-offering an opportunity to cultivate more holistic and integrated approaches to global land stewardship.

title: Tail Connectedness Between Robotics and AI ETFs and Traditional US Assets Under Different Market Conditions: A Quantile VAR Approach
affiliations: University of Sfax, Brunel University London - Department of Economics and Finance and University of Navarra

detail.title: Tail Connectedness Between Robotics and AI ETFs and Traditional US Assets Under Different Market Conditions: A Quantile VAR Approach

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines tail connectedness between various exchange-traded funds (ETFs) focused on artificial intelligence (AI) and some traditional assets such as bonds, equities, Bitcoin, and oil, as well as the VIX uncertainty index, using US daily data over the period from 1 January 2023 to 23 June 2025. The investigation is carried out following the QVAR (Quantile VAR) approach introduced by Ando et al. (2022); this is an extension of the connectedness measure of Diebold and Yilmaz (2012, 2014) which captures the dynamic relationships between assets under different market conditions. The results show that AI and robotics ETFs, along with the S&P 500 Index, act as net transmitters of shocks, while other assets and the VIX serve as net receivers. Furthermore, connectedness intensifies under extreme market conditions. These findings suggest that technology ETFs play a central role in shock transmission and could be effectively employed for hedging purposes. Our findings provide valuable information to investors for diversification and hedging purposes, and to policy makers for maintaining financial stability, particularly during periods of market turbulence.

title: Geopolitical Risk and Global Banking
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Federal Reserve Bank of Boston

detail.title: Geopolitical Risk and Global Banking

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: How do banks respond to geopolitical risk, and is this response distinct from other macroeconomic risks? Using U.S. supervisory data and new geopolitical risk indices, we show that banks reduce cross-border lending to countries with elevated geopolitical risk but continue lending to those markets through foreign affiliates—unlike their response to other macro risks. Furthermore, banks reduce domestic lending when geopolitical risk rises abroad, especially when they operate foreign affiliates. A simple banking model in which geopolitical shocks feature expropriation risk can explain these findings: Foreign funding through affiliates limits downside losses, making affiliate divestment less attractive and amplifying domestic spillovers.

title: Renewable Energy Supply Shocks from Wind Electricity

detail.title: Renewable Energy Supply Shocks from Wind Electricity

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper identifies electricity supply shocks by exploiting the fact that variations in wind speed at turbine locations are exogenous with respect to macroeconomic outcomes and drive electricity prices in European wholesale markets inframarginally. Instrumenting electricity price changes with these wind supply shocks, I find that higher electricity prices raise inflation and reduce electricity use as expected, but generate surprising effects on economic activity. Unemployment rises, but industrial production also rises over time, and the effect on GDP is negligible. As these effects differ markedly from the impact of oil price shocks, they suggest that as economies shift from fossil fuels to renewable electricity, business cycle dynamics may persistently change.

title: Distorted Prices and Targeted Taxes in the New Keynesian Network Model
affiliations: Aix-Marseille-Univ and University of Tübingen - Department of Economics

detail.title: Distorted Prices and Targeted Taxes in the New Keynesian Network Model

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: When confronted with sectoral shocks, policymakers often resort to targeted, sector-specific taxes in an ad hoc fashion. Based on the New Keynesian Network model, we characterize the optimal tax response to sectoral shocks: it features twice as many tax instruments as there are sectors, is budget-neutral, and not confined to the sector where the shock originates. We show that the optimal policy can be approximated by a simple rule that responds to inflation in the shocked sector and adjusts tax instruments in other sectors according to input-output linkages. We study its quantitative performance in a calibrated version of the model.

title: Identity as Self-Image
affiliations: Princeton University - Department of Economics and Erasmus University Rotterdam

detail.title: Identity as Self-Image

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We review the economic literature on self-image, which conceptualizes identity as a set of beliefs about one’s core traits, values, goals, and social ties. Self-image concerns lead individuals to process information and make choices in non-standard ways that help affirm and protect certain valued identities. We first present the main cognitive mechanisms involved within a simple unifying framework. We then survey the extensive laboratory, online, and field experimental literature on the nature and behavioral implications of self-image concerns. We discuss in particular how they give rise to information and decision avoidance, motivated memory and beliefs, excuse-driven behavior, preferences for truth-telling, hypothetical bias, moral cleansing and moral licensing, collective identities, political preferences, and other forms of self-signaling or self-deception. We subsequently discuss common empirical strategies used to identify self-image concerns, as well as the threats to their validity and how to alleviate them. We conclude by outlining open questions and directions for future research on the belief-based approach to identity.

detail.abstract: Perceptions about students’ responsibility for their success might have crucial implications for public approval of targeted financial support. Using a survey experiment among the German adult population, we find that information about the correlation of education outcomes and parental background strongly increases the perception that circumstances determine educational success. These effects persist in a follow-up survey conducted two weeks later. Information also significantly increases private donations to charities supporting students from disadvantaged backgrounds but does not affect demand for governmental redistributive education spending. This pattern is consistent with differences in perceived opportunity costs of funds used in both spending decisions

detail.title: Taxing Corporate or Shareholder Income

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: As corporate income tax rates have fallen across the world, other capital taxes become more important. This paper studies the choice between income taxation at the corporate and shareholder level. I develop a sufficient-statistics framework to determine optimal tax reforms. The main result is that when the incidence of the corporate income tax on workers is higher than that of shareholder income taxes, lowering the former and reducing the latter is typically optimal. In a policy application, I derive optimal reform directions for corporate and shareholder income taxes for a large and a small economy.

detail.title: Work-from-Home and Wage Convergence Across Cities: An Exploration

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper provides evidence on a WFH-related hypothesis that has not previously been tested empirically. The hypothesis is that the presence of fully remote workers, for whom residence and work locations are decoupled, should create a tendency toward wage convergence across cities within teleworkable occupations. The reason is that, since fully remote workers can work anywhere, local wages must match those available in other cities for employers to attract any of these workers. By combining occupational wage data with data on which occupations are teleworkable, the paper attempts to test the wage-convergence hypothesis. The results are mixed, but some evidence does emerge in favor of the hypothesis.

affiliations: Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business and Fudan University

detail.title: Foreign Investment and Corporate Social Responsibility in an Emerging Market: Impacts and Mechanisms
detail.abstract: We examine the causal effect and underlying mechanisms of foreign investment on social norms in an emerging market. Increased foreign investment in Chinese firms under the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Connect programs increases firms’ environmental and social (ES) performance. To isolate underlying mechanisms, we develop an instrumental-variable approach and find causal evidence that supports two theories: foreign investors influence firms to improve ES performance and firms enhance ES performance to signal trustworthiness to investors. Improved ES performance and increased foreign shareholding are therefore self-reinforcing: long-run changes exceed short-run by about 80%. Short-run influence effects are somewhat larger than signalling effects, while both contribute fairly equally to long-run dynamics. Foreign investment can play an important and lasting role in convergence of social norms across countries via either mechanism.

AI.tldr: 该研究探讨了外国投资对中国新兴市场社会规范的因果效应及机制。研究发现沪港通和深港通项目下的外国投资提升了中国企业的环境和社会（ES）绩效，并揭示了两种因果机制：外国投资者影响企业改善ES绩效，以及企业通过提升ES绩效向投资者传递可信信号。
AI.research_question: 外国投资对新兴市场社会规范的因果效应及其作用机制是什么？
AI.motivation: 探讨外国投资如何影响企业环境和社会绩效，以及这种影响背后的理论机制，为理解跨国投资对社会规范的长期影响提供证据。

detail.title: Style Investment and Expected Stock Returns
detail.abstract: Individual investors with different styles hold different opinions about assets. In this study, we first develop a novel measure of style disagreement among retail investors based on the stock message data with machine learning methods. We show that our disagreement measure is negatively (positively) associated with future stock returns (trading volume) in the cross section for the Chinese market. The negative relation between style disagreement and stock returns can be rationalized by a mispricing channel. This study speaks to the literature of style investment and sheds new light on the pricing of stocks in a market populated by retail investors.

title: Covariate Balancing and the Equivalence of Weighting and Doubly Robust Estimators of Average Treatment Effects
affiliations: Brandeis University - International Business School, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) and Michigan State University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Covariate Balancing and the Equivalence of Weighting and Doubly Robust Estimators of Average Treatment Effects

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: How should researchers adjust for covariates? We show that if the propensity score is estimated using a specific covariate balancing approach, inverse probability weighting (IPW), augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW), and inverse probability weighted regression adjustment (IPWRA) estimators are numerically equivalent for the average treatment effect (ATE), and likewise for the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT). The resulting weights are inherently normalized, making normalized and unnormalized IPW and AIPW identical. We discuss implications for instrumental variables and difference-in-differences estimators and illustrate with two applications how these numerical equivalences simplify analysis and interpretation.

AI.tldr: 本文证明当使用特定协变量平衡方法估计倾向得分时，IPW、AIPW和IPWRA估计量在ATE和ATT估计上数值等价，且权重自然归一化，简化了分析和解释。

title: Do individuals accept fluctuations in pension income?
affiliations: ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research, Max Planck Society for the Advancement of the Sciences - Munich Center for the Economics of Aging (MEA), affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Mannheim - Department of Banking and Finance

detail.title: Do individuals accept fluctuations in pension income?
detail.abstract: How to invest and decumulate wealth during retirement has far-reaching consequences for consumption during retirement. We conduct an online experiment in Germany with the objective of understanding preferences for investment and asset decumulation. We investigate the choice between different phased withdrawal plans with varying riskiness resulting in potentially volatile retirement income. We find that 40% of the participants choose some risk and thus, accept fluctuations in retirement income. We analyze the choice between the selected withdrawal plan and a lifelong annuity. Overall, 56% of the respondents choose a life-long annuity. Preferences for an annuity are slightly stronger among individuals who chose the risk-free and medium-risk withdrawal plans as compared to the risky plan. Anchoring and fluctuation frames have small and significant effects on plan choice.

title: When Clicks Replace Trips: Urban Traffic, Welfare, and Environmental Co-Benefits
affiliations: Peking University - National School of Development

detail.title: When Clicks Replace Trips: Urban Traffic, Welfare, and Environmental Co-Benefits
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first causal evidence on how e-commerce affects urban congestion. Exploiting an exogenous surge in online purchases during a major shopping event and instrumenting with pre-event postage costs, I find that a 10% increase in online shopping reduces congestion by 2.9% at peak and 1.5% off-peak. A simple model shows that traffic falls when delivery requires fewer vehicle kilometers than store visits. The underlying mechanisms---mode substitution and logistics efficiency---suggest that similar benefits extend to broader digital adoption. Calibrated to Beijing, the IV estimates imply around CNY 5.5 billion per year in time-related savings from avoided shopping trips plus congestion relief. Environmental co-benefits from reduced local air pollution and CO2 amount to about CNY 0.47--CNY 0.83 billion annually, depending on valuation assumptions.

AI.tldr: 本文首次提供了电子商务对城市拥堵影响的因果证据，发现在线购物增加10%可使高峰拥堵减少2.9%、非高峰减少1.5%，为北京带来每年约55亿元的时间节约和4.7-8.3亿元的环境收益

title: Understanding Firm Behavior in the Green Transition: Insights from Survey Data
affiliations: Atilim University and Atilim University

detail.title: Understanding Firm Behavior in the Green Transition: Insights from Survey Data
detail.abstract: This study investigates the determinants of firm-level green transition using over 15,000 observations from the latest Business Environment and Enterprise Performance Survey (BEEPS), covering 40 countries across Europe, Central Asia, the Middle East, and North Africa. Employing logistic regression models, it quantifies the influence of market pressures, regulatory exposure, organizational capacity, operational conditions, and environmental risk experiences on the probability of adopting green practices. The results identify customer demand for environmental certifications as the strongest predictor, increasing green adoption likelihood by approximately 24 percentage points. Exposure to performance-based regulations, particularly energy performance standards, raises this probability by about 20 percentage points, supporting the Porter Hypothesis on regulation-induced innovation. Organizational capabilities—such as formal environmental strategies, active governance boards, and internationally recognized quality certifications—significantly enhance adoption. Firms directly experiencing environmental damage or CO2 emissions also display higher transition probabilities, with magnitudes varying by institutional context. These findings underscore that effective climate policy must integrate enforceable regulation with measures that leverage market incentives, strengthen governance capacity, and enhance access to green finance. Such coordinated approaches can accelerate corporate environmental transformation, substantially supporting national mitigation targets and international climate commitments.

title: Does the installation of wind farms in Brazil's northeastern municipalities affect the local labor market?
affiliations: Federal University of Ceara, Universidade Federal do Ceara, Federal University of Ceara, Federal University of Ceara and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Does the installation of wind farms in Brazil's northeastern municipalities affect the local labor market?
detail.abstract: In Brazil, most wind farms are located in the Northeast and can contribute to local and regional development by generating temporary and permanent jobs. This article seeks to assess the causal effects of the construction and installation of wind farms on the labor market in municipalities in the Northeast. To this end, annual data from the Northeastern municipalities is used for 1998 to 2022 and, as an empirical strategy, the differences-in-differences (DiD) model with staggered treatment adjustment, proposed by Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021). The results show that municipalities with wind farms have 17.06% more jobs and a 24.75% increase in the wage bill compared to their neighbors without such projects. The dynamic effect shows that the number of jobs is 24.02% higher in the first year after the wind projects come into effect. Similarly, the wage bill variable shows positive and significant effects between the 5th and 8th year after treatment, which may be associated with the plant-building process. Based on the results found, it is clear that the presence of wind farms in northeastern municipalities has the potential to contribute in various ways to regional development.

title: Robust Determinants of Green Finance
affiliations: University of Granada and

detail.title: Robust Determinants of Green Finance
detail.abstract: Green finance is instrumental in helping emerging and developing economies transition to environmentally sustainable practices and address climate change challenges. Nevertheless, robust empirical evidence on its determinants remains limited. This study analyzes the potential and robust determinants of green finance in 93 developing countries from 2000 to 2020. First, we provide an extensive review of existing research on green finance and identify its potential determinants. Second, we determine the robust determinants of green finance by applying a range of estimation techniques, including Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA), LASSO, Elastic Net, Weighted Least Squares, and non-parametric methods (Random Forest and Gradient Boosting). The robust predictors of green finance are globalization, GDP per capita, trade, multilateral flows, climate vulnerability, government effectiveness, rule of law, official development assistance, unemployment, and population. Using these predictors improves the accuracy of out-of-sample forecasts compared to models that include all potential predictors of green finance identified by the literature. By focusing on the identified determinants, policymakers can mobilize green finance more effectively to support climate-resilient development.

title: Proving What Didn't Happen: Redefining Compliance Through Cryptographic Proofs Of Absence
affiliations: Epistria

detail.title: Proving What Didn't Happen: Redefining Compliance Through Cryptographic Proofs Of Absence
detail.abstract: Current compliance infrastructures are built on procedural controls, attestations, and audit logs. These mechanisms can show what happened, but they collapse when regulators, courts, or the public demand proof of what did not happen. This paper introduces a theoretical framework for evidentiary compliance, establishing a taxonomy of cryptographic proof structures that extend assurance beyond activity into absence. Beginning with architectural fairness (Bias-Blind Behavioral Pattern Recognition), the progression advances through destruction receipts (Ephemeral Initialization Vectors), lifecycle receipts (Cryptographic State Transition Proofs), and relational reachability proofs (Relational Merkle Trees, or AuditVerifiable Compliance Receipts). Together, these constructs reframe compliance from a procedural function into an evidentiary discipline capable of withstanding adversarial and legal scrutiny. The framework not only anticipates emerging regulatory mandates but also demonstrates competitive, operational, and ethical advantages for early adopters. Evidentiary compliance marks a paradigm shift: from trust in process to verifiable proof of both events and non-events.

detail.title: Challenges of Intercultural Communication between Japan and Argentina: A Preliminary Review
detail.abstract: This paper explores the dynamics of intercultural communication between Japan and Argentina, with particular attention to how cultural differences shape business relations, media representations, and public perceptions. Drawing on theories of Hall and Hofstede, as well as press coverage and trade data, the study highlights the persistent stereotypes that condition bilateral understanding and the opportunities for deeper dialogue. While Japanese investment and trade with Argentina remain modest compared to Brazil, recent developments suggest an increasing need for strategies that bridge cultural gaps and enhance mutual cooperation. The findings point to the importance of transcending stereotypes through culturally sensitive communication, while also underscoring the lack of systematic research on Japan-Argentina relations. Further studies are needed to explore this underdeveloped field and its implications for Latin American-Japanese cooperation.

title: The Logic of Wealth
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: The Logic of Wealth
detail.abstract:
This paper aims to re-examine and construct a comprehensive framework for wealth analysis in response to the limitations of traditional economic theories in explaining the complexities of modern economies. We propose a multi-dimensional "logic of wealth" framework, which classifies wealth into seven core categories: natural resource wealth, product and service wealth, productive assets, representative wealth, knowledge wealth, relational wealth, and human resource wealth.

The core contributions of this study are threefold. First, it introduces a "survival-pursuit-waste" three-tier structure for product and service wealth, using this as a central focus for understanding macroeconomic operations and highlighting how aggregate growth can conceal structural problems. Second, it systematically analyzes the dynamic logical relationships among the seven wealth categories, especially clarifying the core position of human resource wealth as the creator, consumer, and value assessor, and the decisive role of relational wealth (particularly political institutions) as the "meta-wealth" that governs the creation and distribution of all other forms of wealth. Finally, based on this "logic of wealth," the paper systematically introduces the concept of "negative wealth," mapping it to the seven wealth categories to provide a new "net wealth governance" perspective for economic management.

In conclusion, the framework presented in this paper aims to move beyond traditional market and price analyses. It offers a more structured, systemic, and human-centered tool for macroeconomic governance, with the goal of achieving fairer and more sustainable social well-being.

title: Blackbox Simulation Optimization
affiliations: Fudan University, Fudan University and Fudan University

detail.title: Blackbox Simulation Optimization
detail.abstract: Simulation optimization is a widely used tool in the analysis and optimization of complex stochastic systems. The majority of the previous works on simulation optimization rely heavily on detailed system information, such as the distributions of input variables and the system dynamics. However, it is usually costly and even unrealistic to obtain such detailed information in practice. To overcome this difficulty, new methods are needed to solve stochastic optimization problems based on simulation outputs or real-world data and fairly limited knowledge of the underlying system, i.e., in a blackbox setting. In this paper, we provide an upto-date overview of the subject of blackbox simulation optimization, which has only been attracting attention from the simulation community in recent years. We discuss some of the new stochastic approximation algorithms developed recently for blackbox stochastic optimization. We also discuss challenges and potential future research opportunities.

detail.abstract:
Human beings are uniquely compelled by aspiration. Throughout history, individuals and societies have navigated between abstract visions of what ought to be, subjective convictions of what is worthy, and concrete achievements in the real world. For centuries, these forces have been described in various dyads-means and ends, idea and practice, thought and action. Yet, the triad of ideal, value, and benefit-understood antinomously as mutually tensioned, irreducibly distinct, but necessarily interacting terms-provides a deeper, more nuanced analytic framework for understanding decision-making, ethics, public policy, and personal growth. 

Key Concepts Decision theory and medical decision analysis frameworks; Synonym/antonym structures for value and benefit; Triadic and antinomous reasoning in educational and philosophical literature; Corporate and policy value frameworks. 

*** In what follows, I will explain and defend the triadic, antinomous frame of ideal, value, and benefit. Drawing on philosophy, practical examples, and academic precedent, I demonstrate how this structure clarifies reasoning and strengthens argumentation, and why insisting on the distinction and interplay among these terms is both rational and rhetorically powerful.

title: The Logic of Contract: Resolving the "Contractual Institutional Paradox"
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: The Logic of Contract: Resolving the "Contractual Institutional Paradox"
detail.abstract: This article addresses the evolution of institutional paths, exploring why societies diverge toward either authoritarianism or democracy. Based on a "four-tier contract" framework (Ordinary Contract, Social Normative Contract, Governance Contract, and Meta-Contract), the paper argues that the validity of all lower-tier contracts ultimately depends on the fulfillment of the Meta-Contract. However, since the Meta-Contract lacks a higher enforcement mechanism, its performance logic reverts to the "law of the jungle," thus creating a "contractual institutional paradox." To resolve this dilemma, the article introduces the concepts of "Counterbalancing Power" and "Tamed Law of the Jungle," elucidating how Counterbalancing Power can promote military neutrality, enable compromise, and foster win-win outcomes among competing parties, thereby taming the original logic of violence and driving institutional civilization. By contrasting the gradual constitutional evolution of Britain with the reverse institutional regression in postrevolutionary Iran, the paper shows that when Counterbalancing Power is sufficient, military neutrality is maintained, the Meta-Contract is stably fulfilled, and social progress is driven. Conversely, forced military intervention can weaken Counterbalancing Power, leading to the failure of the meta-contract and institutional backsliding. Finally, the article proposes several strategies to ensure the sustainability of institutional civilization and offers a framework for democratic transitions in authoritarian/totalitarian societies.

detail.abstract: This article introduces and develops the concept of the Digital Invisible Hand, understood as the process through which major technology corporations, by means of algorithmic infrastructures and data monopolies, operate as de facto regulators of both economy and society. Unlike Adam Smith's classical metaphor, grounded in decentralization and diversity of actors, the digital version is marked by concentration, opacity, and the capacity to establish new rules of the game. It is argued that technological announcements made by these corporations possess the power to redefine political agendas, regulatory priorities, and cultural frameworks, shifting initiative from states to the corporate sphere. The article discusses the implications of this dynamic for contemporary leadership, governance, and transitions toward sustainable futures.

detail.abstract:
Healthcare transformation initiatives systematically fail despite decades of re-
form and billions in investment. This paper introduces the Governance Genetic
Engineering (GGE) framework, applying computational biology principles to
organizational DNA. Using abductive reasoning and structural isomorphism anal-
ysis, GGE distinguishes between prevention approaches (governance immunity
engineering for developing systems like Uganda) and intervention approaches
(genetic laboratories for established autoimmune systems like US/UK healthcare).
GGE generates falsifiable predictions about transformation success while offering
practical methodologies for governance immunity engineering.
Healthcare transformation initiatives systematically fail due to governance au-
toimmunity—protective mechanisms that evolved into innovation-attacking anti-
bodies. This paper introduces the Governance Genetic Engineering (GGE) frame-
work, which encompasses governance autoimmune theory (explaining systematic
transformation failures) and governance immunity engineering methodology
(providing prevention and intervention protocols). Governance autoimmune is
the first systematic theory explaining why stakeholder proliferation (from 2 stake-
holders in medieval healthcare to 8+ in modern systems) creates mathematical
inevitability of autoimmune responses that destroy beneficial innovations.
Using abductive reasoning and structural isomorphism analysis, GGE distin-
guishes between prevention approaches (governance immunity engineering for
developing systems) and intervention approaches (genetic laboratories for es-
tablished autoimmune systems). The theory generates testable predictions
about stakeholder thresholds, governance pattern inheritance, and autoimmune
development stages.
GGE provides explanatory power for previously puzzling transformation fail-
ures while offering the first systematic methodology for engineering governance
immunity before dysfunction crystallizes. This represents a paradigm shift
from treating transformation symptoms to preventing governance autoimmune
diseases.
Index Terms: Governance, organizational transformation, healthcare innovation,
digital twins, computational modeling, governance autoimmunity, governance
immunity engineering.
Implementation: The framework enables immediate pilot deployment in Uganda’s
nascent health governance system, preventing autoimmune development at $2M
investment versus $200M+ intervention costs in established systems.

detail.title: Comparative Study of COVID-19's Economic Impact on Different Industries
detail.abstract:
This study aimed to investigate the economic impact of COVID-19 on different industries and compare the effects by looking at certain economic factors and statistics presented by countries such as New Zealand and the UK to compare the post-, pre- and during-COVID-19 conditions of the countries. This is done using quantitative figures provided by the government during certain periods.


We are also going to investigate the impacts on Health New Zealand (Te Whatu Ora), a government agency similar to the National Health Service (NHS). We will compare hospital deaths due to COVID-19 and the overall costs of COVID-19 patients. Further, we will compare pharmaceutical firms’ impacts on relieving the COVID-19 stress on the healthcare systems in the UK and New Zealand.


To begin, we compared and contrasted research done by other journals and researchers, identifying the bases of knowledge already discovered about the economic impact of COVID-19. From this, we identified certain gaps in information and research, these gaps to provide thorough evidence about the economic impact of COVID-19.


In our methodology, we compared many significant variables and took them into account when considering the economic impact of COVID-19 economic impact on our case studies in the UK and New Zealand. The variables range from population and health impact comparison, Healthcare system investment, Trade & economic connectivity and Pharmaceutical figures. These variables allowed us to verify whether our hypothesis was factual or flawed.

detail.title: A Step Toward Democratic ESOPs: A Worker Voice Innovation for Trustee Accountability and Plan Governance
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a voluntary, legally compatible framework to embed employee voice within ESOP governance without statutory change. The core innovation is a Participant Representative, an independent nonfiduciary service provider who conducts structured listening, runs an annual advisory Plan Voice Ballot, and synthesizes results into a plain language stewardship report for the professional trustee. Trustees retain full fiduciary authority under ERISA. The framework creates a procedural audit trail that strengthens prudence records, improves communication, and reduces litigation risk while avoiding any shift in legal control. The model recognizes pass through voting in many C-Corporation ESOPs and targets the distinct needs of S-Corporation ESOPs where voting is centralized in the trustee. The paper details eligibility criteria, disclosure mechanics, record retention, and an escalation review when trustees repeatedly diverge from majority input. It also presents a pilot ready implementation with clear guardrails, an anonymity protocol, and measurable success indicators. The safe harbor concept is voluntary and could be recognized through Department of Labor guidance to create a rebuttable presumption of procedural prudence. Designed to work for smaller ESOPs and to scale to larger companies, the proposal lays a practical foundation for future employee voice systems that may later require legal change.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种自愿的、法律兼容的框架，将员工声音嵌入ESOP治理中，核心创新是引入参与者代表这一独立非受托服务提供商，通过结构化倾听、年度咨询性计划声音投票等方式改善沟通并降低诉讼风险。

detail.abstract: The fiscal effects of foreign aid remain disputed, particularly regarding its effects on domestic tax collection and spending composition. This study investigates the long-run relationship between foreign aid and key fiscal variables-tax revenue, public expenditure, and domestic borrowing-using time series data from Sri Lanka spanning 1959-2018. Employing a cointegrated vector autoregression (CVAR) framework, we find that foreign aid, particularly in the form of loans, is positively associated with capital expenditure and social sector spending, while negatively correlated with recurrent spending and tax effort. Notably, foreign and domestic borrowing jointly appear to disincentivize domestic taxation. These findings suggest that while aid has supported development-oriented spending, it may have inadvertently undermined fiscal sustainability. The Sri Lankan case offers broader insights for aid-dependent and post-conflict developing economies: external financing should be carefully structured to avoid weakening tax effort and to enhance long-term fiscal capacity.

AI.tldr: 本研究使用斯里兰卡1959-2018年的时间序列数据，通过协整向量自回归模型分析外国援助与财政变量（税收、公共支出、国内借款）的长期关系。发现外国援助（特别是贷款形式）与资本支出和社会部门支出正相关，但与经常性支出和税收努力负相关。外国和国内借款共同抑制国内税收，可能削弱财政可持续性。

AI.method: 协整向量自回归（CVAR）框架，使用斯里兰卡1959-2018年的时间序列数据

title: When Anchors Sink Suppliers: Role-Based Asymmetry Bias in AI-Automated Buyer-Supplier Negotiations
affiliations: and

detail.title: When Anchors Sink Suppliers: Role-Based Asymmetry Bias in AI-Automated Buyer-Supplier Negotiations
detail.abstract: Major corporations increasingly deploy AI systems to automate supplier negotiations, optimize pricing strategies, and manage complex commercial relationships. These applications typically assume that large language models (LLMs), trained on broad textual corpora, will perform neutrally, equally capable of representing buyer and supplier interests depending on their assigned role. However, this assumption overlooks potential systematic operational biases that may emerge when AI systems are deployed in different functional roles. We introduce Role-Based Asymmetry Bias: systematic advantages that emerge when AI systems are assigned to different operational roles in strategic interactions. Across two largescale experiments comprising 24,000 bilateral negotiation episodes, we embed multiple LLMs spanning four classes of model sizes in structured buyer-supplier interactions using a controlled newsvendor framework. We observe persistent buyer advantages averaging $11.69 below theoretical equilibrium, representing an 18.6% surplus advantage relative to suppliers. Through turn order manipulation across 16,000 negotiations, we identify a significant anchoring effect ($11.13, SE = 0.40, p < 0.001), demonstrating asymmetric anchoring effectiveness where buyers achieve $11.71 advantages when initiating negotiations while suppliers achieve near-equilibrium outcomes when initiating. This asymmetric pattern reveals that negotiation biases in LLMs operate through differential tactical effectiveness, not just outcome disparities. These findings establish that procedural fairness cannot ensure equitable outcomes when identical negotiation approaches operate asymmetrically based on role assignment, creating hidden competitive risks for organizations deploying AI in strategic business interactions.

AI.tldr: 研究发现AI系统在商业谈判中存在角色不对称偏差，买家角色比供应商角色获得显著优势，这种偏差源于谈判策略的有效性差异而非结果差异。
AI.research_question: AI系统在战略商业互动中是否存在基于角色分配的系统性操作偏差？
AI.motivation: 当前AI系统部署假设LLM在不同角色中表现中性，但忽视了角色分配可能产生的系统性偏差风险。
AI.theoretical_framework: 角色不对称偏差理论、锚定效应理论、战略互动理论
AI.method: 两个大规模实验，包含24,000个双边谈判回合，使用受控报童框架，测试四种不同规模的LLM模型。
AI.findings: 买家获得平均11.69美元的优势（低于理论均衡18.6%），锚定效应显著（11.13美元），买家先发言时优势达11.71美元。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出角色不对称偏差概念，揭示AI谈判偏差通过战术有效性差异而非结果差异运作。
AI.practical_contributions: 警示组织在战略商业互动中部署AI时存在隐藏竞争风险，程序公平无法确保结果公平。

detail.abstract: This paper provides a critical yet complementary response to Dr. Leticia Rodríguez García's chapter Qatar ante la cuestión palestina: apoyo y mediación . It further integrates the concept of “people's diplomacy,” highlighting how grassroots resistance, public opinion, and boycott movements constrain elite-driven normalization. title: Democratizing Optimization with Generative AI
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - School of Engineering, Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School, Microsoft Research and Purdue University

detail.title: Democratizing Optimization with Generative AI
detail.abstract: Recent breakthroughs in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) have captured public imagination, whereas mathematical optimization remains little recognized beyond specialists. In this article, we argue that GenAI can finally bridge the persistent gap between optimization's potent capabilities and its limited real-world uptake. We present the 4I framework-Insight, Interpretability, Interactivity, Improvisation-as a set of design principles for combining GenAI with mathematical optimization. Insight establishes a trusted, up-to-date view of the state; Interpretability explains model logic and trade-offs; Interactivity enables conversational what-if analysis; Improvisation supports event-driven re-optimization. By making optimization tools more intuitive, explainable, and adaptable, we envision a future where frontline decision-makers are empowered to engage in rigorous decision-making. We discuss how GenAI complements, rather than replaces, optimization: GenAI lowers barriers to modeling and interpretation, while mathematical optimization reliably enforces business goals, rules, and hard constraints. We also address emerging concerns, from hallucinations to the risk of over-reliance, and outline research directions to ensure robust, ethical integration of GenAI and optimization. Ultimately, the GenAI boom gives the optimization community a historic opportunity to expand its impact, making decision-intelligence science more accessible and trustworthy to a wider audience while elevating human capabilities.

AI.tldr: 本文提出4I框架（洞察、可解释性、交互性、即兴性），将生成式AI与数学优化相结合，旨在降低优化工具的使用门槛，使一线决策者能够进行严谨的决策分析。

detail.title: Lessons for Antitrust from the Capital One-Discover Merger: Is There a Subprime Market in Credit Cards?

publicationDetails.detailsText: George Mason Law & Economics Research Paper No. 25-12
publicationDetails.journalName: Antonin Scalia Law School, George Mason University, Law & Economics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
In April 2025, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency cleared the proposed $35 billion merger of Capital One and Discover Bank, making the combined company the third-largest credit card issuers by volume. Because of the highly decentralized nature of the U.S. credit card industry, the merger typically would draw minimal regulatory scrutiny. Because of the significant market share of the two entities in the so-called “subprime” credit card market, however, the merger pre-sented a novel question at the intersection of competition policy and consumer financial services—whether the “subprime” market should be analyzed as a separate market for antitrust purposes. According to one estimate the combined entity will have approximately 30% of the subprime market at the time the merger is consummated.

The OCC did not specifically address whether there was a “subprime” market that should be treated as a separate market for purposes of analyzing the effect on consumers and competition. We agree with that analysis. Although the term “subprime” is used colloquially, defining a “sub-prime market” lacks a determinate and stable definition for purposes of rigorous antitrust analysis. Moreover, consumers who participate in the subprime market are subject to constant change and turnover, moving frequently between the subprime and prime markets. Finally, given the permea-bility of any demarcation between “prime” and “subprime” consumers, other large credit card issu-ers already have a presence in the subprime market and could easily expand their existing opera-tions if Capital One-Discover attempted to increase prices for consumers.

AI.tldr: 本文分析了Capital One与Discover Bank合并案在反垄断审查中的关键问题，即是否应将"次级"信用卡市场视为独立市场进行反垄断分析。作者支持OCC的观点，认为"次级"市场缺乏稳定定义，消费者在次级和优质市场间频繁流动，且其他发卡机构已存在并可能扩大业务，因此合并不会显著影响竞争。

AI.theoretical_framework: 基于反垄断经济学理论，特别是市场界定理论和竞争效应分析框架，探讨市场细分在反垄断审查中的适用性。

detail.abstract: Drinkplomacy, a concept coined by Nazar Tretiak (Faculty of European Studies, Babeș-Bolyai University), examines alcohol in negotiations, politics, international relations, and diplomacy. From vodka and wine to champagne and whiskey, drinks have shaped trust, culture, and outcomes at the highest level. The Yalta Conference of 1945 shows how Stalin, Churchill, and Roosevelt turned ritualized drinking into informal diplomacy. Drinkplomacy reframes alcohol not as anecdote but as an institutionalized tool of global politics.

publicationDetails.journalName: European Bank for Reconstruction & Development Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We document how banks' voluntary climate commitments predict both their green lending practices and their borrowers' environmental investments. Using structured surveys of 644 bank CEOs and heads of credit across 33 low-and middle-income countries, we develop indices of banks' green management and lending practices. These unique organizational data reveal that banks signing international climate initiatives (`talk') indeed exhibit stronger green practices (`walk') than non-signatories. We then merge our bank data with detailed surveys of 4,719 firms and show that firms borrowing from climate-committed banks are more likely to undertake green investments. Exploiting geocoded bank branch and firm locations, we further find evidence of spatial matching: environmentally-oriented firms preferentially borrow from climate-committed banks in their vicinity. These patterns are consistent with voluntary climate commitments reflecting genuine environmental orientation rather than greenwashing.

detail.abstract:
Understanding how users authentically interact with Large Language Models (LLMs) remains a significant challenge in human-computer interaction research. Most existing studies rely on self-reported usage patterns or controlled experimental conditions, potentially missing genuine behavioral adaptations. This study presents the first behavioral analysis of Indian Chat-GPT usage based on 238 authentic, unedited user prompts from 40 professional users across 15+ Indian cities, collected via retrospective survey methodology in August 2025. Using authentic prompt collection without observer bias, we analyzed real usage patterns.

Key findings include: 
(1) 85% daily usage rate (34/40 users) indicating mature adoption beyond experimental use, 
(2) 82.1% of users (32/39) demonstrate cross-domain integration spanning professional, personal, health, and creative contexts, 
(3) 42.5% (17/40) primarily use ChatGPT for professional workflows with evidence of real-time problem-solving integration, and 
(4) systematic cultural context navigation strategies with 15.1% of prompts including explicit Indian cultural specifications. 

Users develop sophisticated adaptation techniques and advisory relationship formation for personal guidance. The study reveals progression from experimental to essential workflow dependency, with users treating ChatGPT as an integrated life assistant rather than specialized tool. 

However, findings are limited to English-speaking urban professionals (LinkedIn recruitment bias) and require broader demographic validation. This work contributes a novel methodology for capturing authentic AI usage patterns and provides evidence-based insights into cultural adaptation strategies in emerging markets.

title: Climate Shocks in Global Supply Chains: Lead Time Delay, Inventory Buffering, and Firm Performance
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics,  and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

detail.title: Climate Shocks in Global Supply Chains: Lead Time Delay, Inventory Buffering, and Firm Performance
detail.abstract: Global supply chains face escalating disruptions from climate shocks, yet operational strategies to mitigate their impact remain little understood. Integrating Automatic Identification System (AIS) vessel-tracking data, transaction-level U.S. import shipment records, and quarterly firm financial data, we quantify how hurricanes induce maritime lead-time delays and trace the resulting operational and financial consequences. We reveal that hurricane-induced port disruptions result in an 8-11% increase in transit time, causing reduced quarterly ROA, net profit margin, and total inventories. The inventory channel is central: firms with higher pre-disruption inventory levels suffer significantly smaller profit losses, confirming safety stocks as an operational buffer. Manufacturers-heavily dependent on raw-material inflows-incur disproportionately larger disruptions, whereas larger firms exhibit greater resilience. Overall, our findings underscore the value of inventory buffering in climate-exposed global supply chains and demonstrate how real-time logistics data can be merged with financial outcomes to quantify firm-level supply chain disruption risk.

detail.abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of organizational culture, a concept that, while widely discussed, often remains poorly understood. It examines how culture--defined as the shared values, assumptions and norms guiding organizational behavior--emerged as a central focus of management research beginning in the 1970s. Drawing on multiple research traditions, the chapter reviews major approaches to studying culture: dimensional models, interrelated structure frameworks, and typologies. The chapter evaluates the relationship between organizational culture and performance, including debates about "strong" versus "weak" cultures, the role of adaptability and culture's influence on mergers and external partnerships. While no single cultural profile guarantees success, leaders who understand and shape culture in alignment with strategic goals are better positioned to sustain organizational effectiveness and resilience.

title: Asymmetric Volatility Transmission, Global Fear and Risk-Return Dynamics in the Indian Stock Market: Insights from the U.S. Market and the VIX with Predictive Validation

detail.title: Asymmetric Volatility Transmission, Global Fear and Risk-Return Dynamics in the Indian Stock Market: Insights from the U.S. Market and the VIX with Predictive Validation
detail.abstract: The interconnectedness of global financial markets has increased the transmission of volatility, particularly from developed to emerging economies. This study examines asymmetric volatility spillovers, global fear and the risk-return dynamics of the Indian stock market, with a focus on the influence of the U.S. market and the VIX. Using a series of econometric models, including regression, Arimax, Tgarch, and Garch-in-Mean, the analysis captures return transmission, volatility clustering and asymmetry. Results confirm that S&P 500 returns exert a significant positive influence on Sensex returns, while the VIX negatively impacts returns and contributes to higher volatility. Tgarch highlights the presence of asymmetric spillovers, where negative shocks generate stronger volatility than positive shocks, whereas Garch-in-Mean provides insights into the weak risk-return trade-off in the Indian market. Predictive validation through Arima indicates moderate forecasting reliability, reinforcing the inherent unpredictability of equity markets. These findings provide useful implications for investors and policymakers in assessing cross-market linkages, volatility risks, and the limits of predictive modelling.

detail.abstract: We examine Bitcoin's tail risk within the Basel framework using Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall. Daily data from 2018 to 2024 are analyzed by comparing the Stochastic Volatility with Correlated Jumps (SVCJ) model with its nested specifications and standard GARCH-type benchmarks (Duffie et al., 2000). The SVCJ framework is particularly suitable for cryptocurrencies, as it jointly captures stochastic volatility and correlated jumps in both returns and variance. Empirical results indicate that SVCJ delivers more accurate tail-risk forecasts than alternative models across horizons and confidence levels. To our knowledge, this is the first study to systematically evaluate the SVCJ model for Bitcoin tail risk, underscoring its relevance for robust risk management under Basel standards.

detail.abstract: Future-oriented mental time travel enables humans (and possibly some animal species) to prepare for anticipated or imagined scenarios and challenges and therefore has high adaptive value. As with other cognitive behaviors, there are large inter-individual differences in the use of this function. It is not yet fully clarified in which respect people who act very strategically or with foresight differ from those who tend not to plan ahead or prefer spontaneous solutions, referred to as "strategic" vs. "occasional travelers". As an explanatory model for such inter-individual differences, the self-reinforcement hypothesis of future-oriented mental time travel, which is based on B. F. Skinners behaviorist learning theory, is presented. The self-reinforcement hypothesis is amenable to experimental testing using psychometric and imaging methods. Future-oriented mental time travel is a desirable adaptive cognitive behavior that makes everyday life much more predictable and successful, can protect from potential harm, and facilitate the coping with social and professional challenges and the coping of life crises. The development of future-oriented mental time travel training programs that would stimulate and optimize this essential cognitive behavior in children, adults, elderly people, and patients would be of great educational, preventive, and therapeutic value.

detail.abstract: Organizational change is when there are actions taken by businesses or companies to make changes accordingly. These changes could range from its culture, the technology it uses, and internal processes not to mention but a few. In a post-pandemic world, organizations are continuously making changes to their organizational strategy and culture to cater to both their employees and target audiences. In a VUCA (volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous) world, change is always inevitable, and keeping up with current events and work trends is essential. Gap Inc. for example, a retail-focused organization whose focus was jean apparel has grown over the years, and they have grown through creating several brands over the years such as Old Navy, Banana Republic, Gap, Athleta, intermix, and Hill City. Gap Inc. saw the need to expand their products through the creation of these other brands as a way of maintaining its old customers and bringing in new ones to purchase their products. Due to high demand for products in this retail industry, the warehouse distribution centers have adopted the new use of technology to quicken the process of online delivery when it comes to shopping online. That distribution center uses new technology that is called ORBS to sort and compile orders with multiple items. This way it is easier for the warehouse employees to pack multiple orders since the new machines have already done most of the work required. In this paper I shall be addressing change and change management within organizations I shall also be talking about how organizations deal with resistance to change within employees.

title: Foreign Aid vs. Foreign Direct Investment: Which Is More Effective for Sustainable Development?

detail.title: Foreign Aid vs. Foreign Direct Investment: Which Is More Effective for Sustainable Development?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that the views expressed in this paper are personal and do not necessarily reflect the official position of the National Board of Revenue, Bangladesh. The author has no other competing interests to declare.

detail.abstract: This study looks at how well foreign direct investment (FDI) and foreign aid work together to promote sustainable development in developing countries. Though their contributions to sustainability are still up for debate, both financial flows have historically been crucial to economic growth and the fight against poverty. The effects of foreign aid and FDI are assessed in three areas: economic performance, social development, and environmental sustainability. This is done by using a qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) and thematic synthesis of secondary data from sources such as the World Bank, UNCTAD, OECD, and United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) indicators. The recent worldwide drops in investment inflows show how sensitive FDI is to outside shocks, but the results show that it is still a major driver of economic growth, especially through technology transfer, industrial expansion and capital accumulation. Foreign aid has a greater and more immediate impact on social development, particularly in the areas of gender equality, health and education; but its longterm effects are constrained by the risks of dependency and poor management. However, neither flow substantially closes the widening climate financing gap, and neither is adequate to address environmental sustainability. Overall, the study indicates that institutional strength, governance quality and policy alignment with sustainability goals all play a role in the effectiveness of foreign aid and FDI, which is highly context-dependent. Instead of arguing over which flow is better, the findings show that the most promising way to achieve the SDGs is through their complementarity, which uses FDI to spur growth and foreign aid to strengthen social systems.

AI.tldr: 本研究探讨外国直接投资（FDI）和外国援助在发展中国家的协同作用，通过定性比较分析和主题综合评估它们在经济发展、社会发展和环境可持续性三个领域的影响。研究发现FDI主要通过技术转移、工业扩张和资本积累促进经济增长，而外国援助在社会发展方面影响更直接但长期效果受限。两者在环境可持续性方面贡献有限，且效果高度依赖制度强度、治理质量和政策协调。

AI.motivation: 尽管FDI和外国援助对可持续发展的贡献仍有争议，但历史上这两种资金流动对经济增长和减贫至关重要。全球投资流入下降显示FDI对外部冲击敏感，需要系统评估其协同效应。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于可持续发展理论框架，从经济发展、社会发展和环境可持续性三个维度构建分析框架，考虑制度强度、治理质量和政策协调等调节因素。

title: Words That Mean Change: Paradoxical Thinking and Eco-Efficiency in the Automotive Sector
affiliations: Macquarie University, Macquarie Business School and ESCP Business School

detail.title: Words That Mean Change: Paradoxical Thinking and Eco-Efficiency in the Automotive Sector
detail.abstract: This study uses the automotive industry to investigate the link between paradoxical thinking language in corporate sustainability reports and companies' eco-efficiency. We hypothesized that different types of paradoxical thinking would be associated with varying eco-efficiency outcomes. Using ChatGPT to generate a lexicon of paradoxical terms, we analyzed sustainability reports from the automotive industry spanning 2002 to 2022, testing associations with four eco-efficiency indicators. Our analysis reveals that paradoxical thinking matters, but different forms have varying degrees and forms of impact. Specifically, we find that cautious, conditional, and risk-aware language correlates with higher eco-efficiency, while growth-focused and innovationoriented language correlates with lower eco-efficiency. Companies using deliberative, uncertain language achieve superior environmental and economic balance, while those emphasizing expansion and bold innovation show weaker eco-efficiency performance. This research suggests that specific language patterns in sustainability reports both reflect and potentially influence practical environmental outcomes, suggesting that paradoxical thinking is not uniform but varies significantly in its environmental consequences. This is an open access article under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits use, distribution and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited.

detail.title: Asylum Seekers, New Businesses, and Job Creation

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: How do asylum seekers affect host-country economies from a supply and demand perspective? What share of such immigration shocks is absorbed by existing vs. new businesses? To study these questions, we combine exclusive business registration and asylum seeker data for the universe of German districts over 2007-2021. We address endogeneity in asylum seeker allocation by exploiting rule-based allocation quotas as an instrument. A one SD treatment (10 asylum seekers/1,000 inhabitants) leads to 0.7 new businesses (7.9% increase) including 2.7 full-time jobs per 1,000 inhabitants. A sector-level analysis suggests that the founding of new businesses is both supply- (additional workforce) and demand-driven (need for basic goods/services), while the demand effect kicks in first. District-level employment data shows that total job creation is about four times larger, suggesting that 75% of the immigration shock is absorbed by existing businesses.

AI.tldr: 该研究利用德国2007-2021年地区层面的企业注册和寻求庇护者数据，分析寻求庇护者对东道国经济的供给和需求影响。研究发现，寻求庇护者既通过提供额外劳动力（供给效应）又通过创造对基本商品/服务的需求（需求效应）促进新企业创立，其中需求效应先于供给效应显现。现有企业吸收了约75%的移民冲击。

title: Tread with Care
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Tread with Care

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: With increasing debt vulnerabilities, domestic debt may become an important—though still distinct––part of debt restructurings. This paper aims to contribute to the discourse by examining the factors that precipitate domestic debt restructurings (DDRs) and their implications for macro-fiscal outcomes. We find that: (i) DDRs are less effective than external debt restructurings (EDRs) in reducing public debt and interest payments; and (ii) they entail deeper, more persistent costs to output and domestic credit. Still, well-designed DDRs can be critical for restoring macroeconomic stability and sustainability, regardless of costs. Their impacts depend on design, instruments, sovereign-bank nexus, concurrent fiscal consolidation, and financial development. Finally, the paper shows that gross international reserves and the presence of an IMF-supported program can mitigate the costs associated with DDRs while preserving their debt relief benefits.

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Identifying the natural person who ultimately owns or controls an asset—known as the beneficial owner—is a key transparency measure to prevent misuse for criminal or unethical purposes. This is especially critical in high-risk sectors, where vulnerabilities are amplified during economic or existential crises, such as financial bubbles or climate change. While many countries are establishing centralized beneficial ownership registries—often linked to commercial registers for anti-money laundering/combating the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance—these may not fully meet the needs of sector-specific oversight. Agencies like procurement authorities or land registries often require more granular or tailored beneficial ownership data, such as information on foreign entities or lower thresholds for politically exposed persons (PEPs). A sectoral approach to beneficial ownership transparency addresses these gaps by aligning data collection and use with the unique risks and operational realities of each sector. This allows for flexible implementation—from basic disclosures in transactions to advanced verification—while complementing national beneficial ownership frameworks. Importantly, the design should consider sectoral capacity and minimize compliance burdens. Drawing on lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, where beneficial ownership transparency in procurement helped mitigate corruption risks, this approach is now being explored for other high-risk areas such as real estate, which is particularly vulnerable to money laundering.

affiliations: , , International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Macroeconomic Exposure to the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Taking the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) as given, our paper evaluates the impact of this terms-of-trade shock on the Middle East and Central Asia (ME&CA). Using a novel methodology and fresh data applied to the latest CBAM legislation, we both quantify and decompose the financial burden countries face as their exports to the EU become subject to a greenhouse gas-based fee starting in January 2026. Our analysis reveals that while the average effects of CBAM in ME&CA are modest, the region will shoulder one of the highest burdens worldwide, totaling US$1.7 billion annually (equivalent to 0.03 percent of GDP and a 14 percent surcharge on CBAM exports to the EU). The Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan (MENAP) subregion will bear a greater share of this burden than the Caucasus and Central Asia (CCA) due to stronger trade ties with the EU and higher emission intensity. Substantial country- and sector-level differences in CBAM exposure emphasize the need for tailored policy responses to mitigate the broader macroeconomic effects.

title: Patterns of Invoicing Currency in Global Trade in a Fragmenting World Economy
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), , International Monetary Fund (IMF), European Central Bank (ECB), International Monetary Fund (IMF) and European Central Bank (ECB)

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper presents the most comprehensive and up-to-date panel dataset on global trade invoicing currency and examines recent pattern shifts with a focus on geopolitical alignment. Using data for 132 countries from 1990 to 2023—including new coverage of the Chinese renminbi—we document five key findings. First, the US dollar remains dominant, with global invoicing shares broadly stable. Second, renminbi use has grown steadily and expanded beyond Asia, though it remains modest. Third, countries not geopolitically aligned with the US continue to rely on the dollar, though this reliance has declined in a few key economies. Fourth, since 2021, the correlation between the use of a given invoicing currency and the geopolitical distance to its issuer has become more negative, reflecting growing polarization. Fifth, there is no robust evidence consistent with effective policy initiatives to reduce dollar reliance in oil exports. These findings highlight the resilience of dominant currencies and suggest emerging fragmentation in invoicing patterns along geopolitical lines.

detail.title: Relocation of Global Value Chains

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The paper documents recent changes in trade flow dynamics between Mexico, the U.S. and China, focusing on the period around 2017-2023. Using product-level bilateral trade data, the paper studies recent trends in the composition of the origin of U.S. imports, notably that a reduction of imports from China has been accompanied by an increase in imports from Mexico and other trading partners in Asia. The paper also documents that while Mexican exports to the U.S. have significantly increased in recent years, Mexico is also importing more from the U.S. and various countries in Asia, consistent with Mexico’s deeper integration into global value chains. Furthermore, the paper presents evidence that FDI flows to Mexico since 2017, predominantly originated from the U.S., have increased more in economic sectors affected by the U.S. tariffs on imports from China, and that they have been mainly directed to regions in the North with well-established manufacturing networks with the U.S.

AI.tldr: 该论文分析了2017-2023年间墨西哥、美国和中国之间贸易流动的变化，发现美国从中国进口减少的同时从墨西哥和其他亚洲贸易伙伴进口增加，墨西哥更深融入全球价值链，且美国对墨西哥的FDI流向受中美贸易战影响的行业和北部制造业地区。

title: Did R&D Misallocation Contribute to Slower Growth?

detail.title: Did R&D Misallocation Contribute to Slower Growth?

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper provides evidence that rising misallocation in the R&D sector contributed to the recent slowdown in U.S. productivity growth. I develop a growth accounting framework allowing for misallocation of R&D resources across firms captured by wedges between their marginal cost and benefits of R&D. I show that R&D wedges can be measured from R&D returns and document large and persistent differences in R&D returns across US-listed firms. Combining data and model, I estimate that frictions reduced productivity growth by 18% over 1975–2014 and that rising misallocation in the R&D sector accounts for 25% of the growth slowdown.
